anopheles: A genus of mosquitoes which are secondary hosts of the malaria parasites, and whose bite is the usual, if not the only, means of infecting human beings with malaria. Several species are found in the United States.
anacardium: A genus of plants including the cashew tree. See Cashew.
antapoplectic: Good against apoplexy. -- n. A medicine used against apoplexy.
anthropical: Like or related to man; human. Owen.
antheriferous: (a) Producing anthers, as plants. (b) Supporting anthers, as a part of a flower. Gray.
antherozoid: One of the mobile male reproductive bodies in the antheridia of cryptogams.
annex: 1. To join or attach; usually to subjoin; to affix; to append; -- followed by to. "He annexed a codicil to a will." Johnson. 2. To join or add, as a smaller thing to a greater. | Something annexed or appended; as, an additional stipulation to a writing, a subsidiary building to a main building; a wing.
anemonin: An acrid, poisonous, crystallizable substance, obtained from some species of anemone.
anthraxvaccine: A fluid vaccine obtained by growing a bacterium (Bacterium anthracis) in beef broth. It is used to immunize animals, esp. cattle.
angolapea: A tropical plant (Cajanus indicus) and its edible seed, a kind of pulse; -- so called from Angola in Western Africa. Called also pigeon pea and Congo pea.
annihilate: 1. To reduce to nothing or nonexistence; to destroy the existence of; to cause to cease to be. It impossible for any body to be utterly annihilated. Bacon. 2. To destroy the form or peculiar distinctive properties of, so that the specific thing no longer exists; as, to annihilate a forest by cutting down the trees. "To annihilate the army." Macaulay. 3.
anhima: A South American aquatic bird; the horned screamer or kamichi (Palamedea cornuta). See Kamichi.
analepsy: (a) Recovery of strength after sickness. (b) A species of epileptic attack, originating from gastric disorder.
anachronism: A misplacing or error in the order of time; an error in chronology by which events are misplaced in regard to each other, esp. one by which an event is placed too early; falsification of chronological relation.
anonymously: In an anonymous manner; without a name. Swift.
antihydrophobic: Counteracting or preventing hydrophobia. -- n. A remedy for hydrophobia.
annulate: 1. Furnished with, or composed of, rings; ringed; surrounded by rings of color. 2. (Zoöl.) Of or pertaining to the Annulata.
antagonist: 1. One who contends with another, especially in combat; an adversary; an opponent. Antagonist of Heaven's Almigthy King. Milton. Our antagonists in these controversies. Hooker. 2. | Antagonistic; opposing; counteracting; as, antagonist schools of philosophy.
ante: A Latin preposition and prefix; akin to Gr. anti, Goth. and-, anda- (only in comp.), AS. and-, ond-, (only in comp.: cf. Answer, Along), G. ant-, ent- (in comp.). The Latin ante is generally used in the sense of before, in regard to position, order, or time, and the Gr. opposite, or in the place of.
ankylosis: 1. (Med.) Stiffness or fixation of a joint; formation of a stiff joint. Dunglison. 2. (Anat.) The union of two or more separate bones to from a single bone; the close union of bones or other structures in various animals.
antizymotic: Preventing fermentation or decomposition. -- n. An agent so used.
anserine: 1. Pertaining to, or resembling, a goose, or the skin of a goose. 2. (Zoöl.) Pertaining to the Anseres.
announcement: The act of announcing, or giving notice; that which announces; proclamation; publication.
antitrochanter: An articular surface on the ilium of birds against which the great trochanter of the femur plays.
androus: A terminal combining form: Having a stamen or stamens; staminate; as, monandrous, with one stamen; polyandrous, with many stamens.
anorthopia: Distorted vision, in which straight lines appear bent.
anabaptistic: Relating or attributed to the Anabaptists, or their doctrines. Milton. Bp. Bull.
antilogy: A contradiction between any words or passages in an author. Sir W. Hamilton.
anecdotist: One who relates or collects anecdotes.
anaerobia: Anaërobic bacteria. They are called facultative anaërobia when able to live either in the presence or absence of free oxygen; obligate, or obligatory, anaërobia when they thrive only in its absence.
anatomy: 1. The art of dissecting, or artificially separating the different parts of any organized body, to discover their situation, structure, and economy; dissection. 2. The science which treats of the structure of organic bodies; anatomical structure or organization.
antipathetical: Having a natural contrariety, or constitutional aversion, to a thing; characterized by antipathy; -- often followed by to. Fuller.
anient: To frustrate; to bring to naught; to annihilate. (old) Chaucer.
antediluvial: Before the flood, or Deluge, in Noah's time.
antegg: One of the small white egg-shaped pupæ or cocoons of the ant, often seen in or about ant-hills, and popularly supposed to be eggs.
angio: A prefix, or combining form, in numerous compounds, usually relating to seed or blood vessels, or to something contained in, or covered by, a vessel.
antepenultima: The last syllable of a word except two, as -syl in monosyllable.
anorthite: A mineral of the feldspar family, commonly occurring in small glassy crystals, also a constituent of some igneous rocks. It is a lime feldspar. See Feldspar.
angulation: A making angular; angular formation. Huxley.
anaglyph: Any sculptured, chased, or embossed ornament worked in low relief, as a cameo.
antero: A combining form meaning anterior, front; as, antero-posterior, front and back; antero-lateral, front side, anterior and at the side.
androgynous: 1. Uniting both sexes in one, or having the characteristics of both; being in nature both male and female; hermaphroditic. Owen. The truth is, a great mind must be androgynous. Coleridge. 2. (Bot.) Bearing both staminiferous and pistilliferous flowers in the same cluster.
antidotical: Serving as an antidote. -- An`ti*dot"ic*al*ly, adv.
ancome: A small ulcerous swelling, coming suddenly; also, a whitlow. (old) Boucher.
anhele: To pant; to be breathlessly anxious or eager (for). (old) They anhele . . . for the fruit of our convocation. Latimer.
anomalistic: 1. Irregular; departing from common or established rules. 2. (Astron.) Pertaining to the anomaly, or angular distance of a planet from its perihelion. Anomalistic month. See under Month. -- Anomalistic revolution, the period in which a planet or satellite goes through the complete cycles of its changes of anomaly, or from any point in its elliptic orbit to the same again.
antitheist: A disbeliever in the existence of God.
antiochian: 1. Pertaining to Antiochus, a contemporary with Cicero, and the founder of a sect of philosophers. 2. Of or pertaining to the city of Antioch, in Syria. Antiochian epoch (Chron.), a method of computing time, from the proclamation of liberty granted to the city of Antioch, about the time of the battle of Pharsalia, B.C. 48.
antipyretic: Efficacious in preventing or allaying fever. -- n. A febrifuge.
andiron: A utensil for supporting wood when burning in a fireplace, one being placed on each side; a firedog; as, a pair of andirons.
antiquate: To make old, or obsolete; to make antique; to make old in such a degree as to put out of use; hence, to make void, or abrogate. Christianity might reasonably introduce new laws, and antiquate or abrogate old one. Sir M. Hale.
angelize: To raise to the state of an angel; to render angelic. It ought not to be our object to angelize, nor to brutalize, but to humanize man. W. Taylor.
antiptosis: The putting of one case for another.
anthrenus: A genus of small beetles, several of which, in the larval state, are very destructive to woolen goods, fur, etc. The common "museum pest" is A. varius; the carpet beetle is A. scrophulariæ. The larvæ are commonly confounded with moths.
anchorage: 1. The act of anchoring, or the condition of lying at anchor. 2. A place suitable for anchoring or where ships anchor; a hold for an anchor. 3. The set of anchors belonging to a ship. 4. Something which holds like an anchor; a hold; as, the anchorages of the Brooklyn Bridge. 5. Something on which one may depend for security; ground of trust. 6. A toll for anchoring;
andromede: A meteor appearing to radiate from a point in the constellation Andromeda, -- whence the name. A shower of these meteors takes place every year on November 27th or 28th. The Andromedes are also called Bielids, as they are connected with Biela's comet and move in its orbit.
anticous: Facing toward the axis of the flower, as in the introrse anthers of the water lily.
antinational: Antagonistic to one's country or nation, or to a national government.
antitoxin: A substance (sometimes the product of a specific micro-organism and sometimes naturally present in the blood or tissues of an animal), capable of producing immunity from certain diseases, or of counteracting the poisonous effects of pathogenic bacteria.
angiography: A description of blood vessels and lymphatics.
anticlinal: The crest or line in which strata slope or dip in opposite directions.
antithesis: 1. (Rhet.) An opposition or contrast of words or sentiments occurring in the same sentence; as, "The prodigal robs his heir; the miser robs himself." "He had covertly shot at Cromwell; he how openly aimed at the Queen." 2. The second of two clauses forming an antithesis. 3. Opposition; contrast.
anisostemonous: Having unequal stamens; having stamens different in number from the petals.
antbear: An edentate animal of tropical America (the Tamanoir), living on ants. It belongs to the genus Myrmecophaga.
analepsis: (a) Recovery of strength after sickness. (b) A species of epileptic attack, originating from gastric disorder.
anastrophe: An inversion of the natural order of words; as, echoed the hills, for, the hills echoed.
anthropomancy: Divination by the entrails of human being.
annexation: 1. The act of annexing; process of attaching, adding, or appending; the act of connecting; union; as, the annexation of Texas to the United States, or of chattels to the freehold. 2. (a) (Law) The union of property with a freehold so as to become a fixture. Bouvier. (b) (Scots Law) The appropriation of lands or rents to the crown. Wharton.
anacrusis: A prefix of one or two unaccented syllables to a verse properly beginning with an accented syllable.
angulous: Angular; having corners; hooked. Held together by hooks and angulous involutions. Glanvill.
anthraconite: A coal-black marble, usually emitting a fetid smell when rubbed; -- called also stinkstone and swinestone.
anchorescapement: (a) The common recoil escapement. (b) A variety of the lever escapement with a wide impulse pin.
anbury: 1. (Far.) A soft tumor or bloody wart on horses or oxen. 2. A disease of the roots of turnips, etc.; -- called also fingers and toes.
antlered: Furnished with antlers. The antlered stag. Cowper.
ankus: An elephant goad with a sharp spike and hook, resembling a short-handled boat hook. [India] Kipling.
anoxemia: An abnormal condition due to deficient aëration of the blood, as in balloon sickness, mountain sickness. -- An`ox*æ"mic, *e"mic (#), a.
anglicity: The state or quality of being English.
anallantoic: Without, or not developing, an allantois.
antispasmodic: Good against spasms. -- n. A medicine which prevents or allays spasms or convulsions.
angora: A city of Asia Minor (or Anatolia) which has given its name to a goat, a cat, etc. Angora cat (Zoöl.), a variety of the domestic cat with very long and silky hair, generally of the brownish white color. Called also Angola cat. See Cat. -- Angora goat (Zoöl.), a variety of the domestic goat, reared for its long silky hair, which is highly prized for manufacture.
ana: Of each; an equal quantity; as, wine and honey, ana (or, contracted, aa), ., that is, of wine and honey, each, two ounces. An apothecary with a . . . long bill of anas. Dryden. | A suffix to names of persons or places, used to denote a collection of notable sayings, literary gossip, anecdotes, etc. Thus, Scaligerana is a book containing the sayings of Scaliger, Johnsoniana of…
anarchist: An anarch; one who advocates anarchy of aims at the overthrow of civil government.
angoumoismoth: A small moth (Gelechia cerealella) which is very destructive to wheat and other grain. The larva eats out the inferior of the grain, leaving only the shell.
analemma: 1. (Chem.) An orthographic projection of the sphere on the plane of the meridian, the eye being supposed at an infinite distance, and in the east or west point of the horizon. 2. An instrument of wood or brass, on which this projection of the sphere is made, having a movable horizon or cursor; -- formerly much used in solving some common astronomical problems. 3.
angler: 1. One who angles. 2. (Zoöl.) A fish (Lophius piscatorius), of Europe and America, having a large, broad, and depressed head, with the mouth very large. Peculiar appendages on the head are said to be used to entice fishes within reach. Called also fishing frog, frogfish, toadfish, goosefish, allmouth, monkfish, etc.
antiquary: Pertaining to antiquity. "Instructed by the antiquary times." Shak. | One devoted to the study of ancient times through their relics, as inscriptions, monuments, remains of ancient habitations, statues, coins, manuscripts, etc.; one who searches for and studies the…
animative: Having the power of giving life or spirit. Johnson.
anagrammatic: Pertaining to, containing, or making, anagram. -- An`a*gram*mat"ic*al*ly, adv.
antipodagric: Good against gout. -- n. A medicine for gout.
antinomian: Of or pertaining to the Antinomians; opposed to the doctrine that the moral law is obligatory. | One who maintains that, under the gospel dispensation, the moral law is of no use or obligation, but that faith alone is necessary to salvation. The sect of Antinomians originated with John Agricola,…
anthology: 1. A discourses on flowers. 2. A collection of flowers; a garland. 3. A collection of flowers of literature, that is, beautiful passages from authors; a collection of poems or epigrams; -- particularly applied to a collection of ancient Greek epigrams. 4. (Gr. Ch.) A service book containing a selection of pieces for the festival services.
anybody: 1. Any one out of an indefinite number of persons; anyone; any person. His Majesty could not keep any secret from anybody. Macaulay. 2. A person of consideration or standing. [Colloq.] All the men belonged exclusively to the mechanical and shopkeeping classes, and there was not a single banker or anybody in the list. Lond. Sat. Rev.
annotine: A bird one year old, or that has once molted.
anatron: 1. Native carbonate of soda; natron. 2. Glass gall or sandiver. 3. Saltpeter. Coxe. Johnson.
angina: Any inflammatory affection of the throat or faces, as the quinsy, malignant sore throat, croup, etc., especially such as tends to produce suffocation, choking, or shortness of breath. Angina pectoris, a peculiarly painful disease, so named from a sense of suffocating contraction or tightening of the lower part of the chest; -- called also breast pang, spasm of the chest.
anabranch: A branch of a river that reënters, or anastomoses with, the main stream; also, less properly, a branch which loses itself in sandy soil. [Australia] Such branches of a river as after separation reunite, I would term anastomosing branches; or, if a word might be coined, anabranches, and the islands they form branch islands. Col. Jackson.
anchored: 1. Held by an anchor; at anchor; held safely; as, an anchored bark; also, shaped like an anchor; forked; as, an anchored tongue. 2. (Her.) Having the extremities turned back, like the flukes of an anchor; as, an anchored cross. [Sometimes spelt ancred.]
anecdotic: Pertaining to, consisting of, or addicted to, anecdotes. "Anecdotical traditions." Bolingbroke.
antecede: To go before in time or place; to precede; to surpass. Sir M. Hale.
ance: A suffix signifying action; also, quality or state; as, assistance, resistance, appearance, elegance. See -ancy. Note: All recently adopted words of this class take either -ance or - ence, according to the Latin spelling.
antholite: A fossil plant, like a petrified flower.
anear: Near. "It did not come anear." Coleridge. The measure of misery anear us. I. Taylor.
anagrammatism: The act or practice of making anagrams. Camden.
anthotaxy: The arrangement of flowers in a cluster; the science of the relative position of flowers; inflorescence.
antihysteric: Counteracting hysteria. -- n. A remedy for hysteria.
anaks: A race of giants living in Palestine.
annual: 1. Of or pertaining to a year; returning every year; coming or happening once in the year; yearly. The annual overflowing of the river [Nile]. Ray. 2. Performed or accomplished in a year; | 1. A thing happening or returning yearly; esp. a literary work published once a year. 2. Anything, especially a plant, that lasts but one year or season; an annual plant. Oaths . . .
antihemorrhagic: Tending to stop hemorrhage. -- n. A remedy for hemorrhage.
anhelation: Short and rapid breathing; a panting; asthma. Glanvill.
anemogram: A record made by an anemograph.
anaesthetic: (a) Capable of rendering insensible; as, anæsthetic agents. (b) Characterized by, or connected with, insensibility; as, an anæsthetic effect or operation. | That which produces insensibility to pain, as chloroform, ether, etc.
any: 1. One indifferently, out of an indefinite number; one indefinitely, whosoever or whatsoever it may be. Note: Any is often used in denying or asserting without limitation; | To any extent; in any degree; at all. You are not to go loose any longer. Shak. Before you go any farther. Steele.
anthropophaginian: One who east human flesh. [Ludicrous] Shak.
anthropic: Like or related to man; human. Owen.
anacanths: A group of teleostean fishes destitute of spiny fin-rays, as the cod.
antiparallel: Running in a contrary direction. Hammond.
annuloida: A division of the Articulata, including the annelids and allied groups; sometimes made to include also the helminths and echinoderms. [Written also Annuloidea.]
andromed: A meteor appearing to radiate from a point in the constellation Andromeda, -- whence the name. A shower of these meteors takes place every year on November 27th or 28th. The Andromedes are also called Bielids, as they are connected with Biela's comet and move in its orbit.
anthropidae: The group that includes man only.
anthophore: The stipe when developed into an internode between calyx and corolla, as in the Pink family. Gray.
antisepalous: Standing before a sepal, or calyx leaf.
antcattle: Various kinds of plant lice or aphids tended by ants for the sake of the honeydew which they secrete. See Aphips.
anaglyptograph: An instrument by which a correct engraving of any embossed object, such as a medal or cameo, can be executed. Brande & C.
anights: In the night time; at night. (old) Does he hawk anights still Marston.
animator: One who, or that which, animates; an animater. Sir T. Browne.
ann: A half years's stipend, over and above what is owing for the incumbency, due to a minister's heirs after his decease.
anaplasty: The art of operation of restoring lost parts or the normal shape by the use of healthy tissue.
annularity: Annular condition or form; as, the annularity of a nebula. J. Rogers.
antipole: The opposite pole; anything diametrically opposed. Geo. Eliot.
anent: 1. Over against; as, he lives anent the church. 2. About; concerning; in respect; as, he said nothing anent this particular.
anneal: 1. To subject to great heat, and then cool slowly, as glass, cast iron, steel, or other metal, for the purpose of rendering it less brittle; to temper; to toughen. 2. To heat, as glass, tiles, or earthenware, in order to fix the colors laid on them.
antibody: Any of various bodies or substances in the blood which act in antagonism to harmful foreign bodies, as toxins or the bacteria producing the toxins. Normal blood serum apparently contains variousantibodies, and the introduction of toxins or of foreign cells also results in the development of their specific antibodies.
antiscorbutic: Counteracting scurvy. -- n. A remedy for scurvy.
anergy: Lack of energy; inactivity. -- An*er"gic (#), a.
anharmonic: Not harmonic. The anharmonic function or ratio of four points abcd on a straight line is the quantity (ac/ad):(bc/bd), where the segments are to regarded as plus or minus, according to the order of the letters.
andantino: Rather quicker than andante; between that allegretto. Note: Some, taking andante in its original sense of "going," and andantino as its diminutive, or "less going," define the latter as slower than andante.
analogize: To employ, or reason by, analogy.
angling: The act of one who angles; the art of fishing with rod and line. Walton.
antiquarian: Pertaining to antiquaries, or to antiquity; as, antiquarian literature. | 1. An antiquary. 2. A drawing paper of large size. See under Paper, n.
antilopine: Of or relating to the antelope.
anhydrite: A mineral of a white a slightly bluish color, usually massive. It is anhydrous sulphate of lime, and differs from gypsum in not containing water (whence the name).
anemonic: An acrid, poisonous, crystallizable substance, obtained from, the anemone, or from anemonin.
anomural: Irregular in the character of the tail or abdomen; as, the anomural crustaceans. [Written also anomoural, anomouran.]
an: This word is properly an adjective, but is commonly called the indefinite article. It is used before nouns of the singular number only, and signifies one, or any, but somewhat less emphatically. | If; -- a word used by old English authors. Shak. Nay, an thou dalliest, then I am thy foe. B. Jonson. An if, and if; if.
angevine: Of or pertaining to Anjou in France. -- n. A native of Anjou.
aniline: An organic base belonging to the phenylamines. It may be regarded as ammonia in which one hydrogen atom has been replaced by the radical phenyl. It is a colorless, oily liquid, originally obtained… | Made from, or of the nature of, aniline.
annul: 1. To reduce to nothing; to obliterate. Light, the prime work of God, to me's extinct. And all her various objects of delight Annulled. Milton. 2. To make void or of no effect; to nullify; to abolish; to do away with;
anatropous: Having the ovule inverted at an early period in its development, so that the chalaza is as the apparent apex; -- opposed to orthotropous. Gray.
antimason: One opposed to Freemasonry. -- An`ti*ma*son"ic, a.
anthroposophy: Knowledge of the nature of man; hence, human wisdom.
angustation: The act or making narrow; a straitening or contacting. Wiseman.
antasthmatic: Opposing, or fitted to relieve, asthma. -- n. A remedy for asthma.
androdioecious: Having perfect and staminate flowers on different plants. -- An`dro*di*o"cism, -di*e"cism (#), n.
anthropomorphist: One who attributes the human form or other human attributes to the Deity or to anything not human.
antitrade: A tropical wind blowing steadily in a direction opposite to the trade wind.
annumerate: To add on; to count in. (old) Wollaston.
androdiecious: Having perfect and staminate flowers on different plants. -- An`dro*di*o"cism, -di*e"cism (#), n.
andesite: An eruptive rock allied to trachyte, consisting essentially of a triclinic feldspar, with pyroxene, hornblende, or hypersthene.
anarchy: 1. Absence of government; the state of society where there is no law or supreme power; a state of lawlessness; political confusion. Spread anarchy and terror all around. Cowper. 2. Hence, confusion or disorder, in general. There being then . . . an anarchy, as I may term it, in authors and their reFuller.
antiphlogistian: An opposer of the theory of phlogiston.
anacamptic: Reflecting of reflected; as, an anacamptic sound (and echo). Note: The word was formerly applied to that part of optics which treats of reflection; the same as what is now called catoptric. See Catoptrics.
anamorphoscope: An instrument for restoring a picture or image distorted by anamorphosis to its normal proportions. It usually consists of a cylindrical mirror.
anorthic: Having unequal oblique axes; as, anorthic crystals.
annodated: Curved somewhat in the form of the letter S. Cussans.
antiquitarian: An admirer of antiquity. Note: [Used by Milton in a disparaging sense.] (old)
anthracosis: A chronic lung disease, common among coal miners, due to the inhalation of coal dust; -- called also collier's lung and miner's phthisis.
antipeptone: A product of gastric and pancreatic digestion, differing from hemipeptone in not being decomposed by the continued action of pancreatic juice.
anchylose: To affect or be affected with anchylosis; to unite or consolidate so as to make a stiff joint; to grow together into one. [Spelt also ankylose.] Owen.
antiburgher: One who seceded from the Burghers (1747), deeming it improper to take the Burgess oath.
anchorspace: In the balk-line game, any of eight spaces, 7 inches by 3½, lying along a cushion and bisected transversely by a balk line. Object balls in an anchor space are treated as in balk.
anarthrous: 1. (Gr. Gram.) Used without the article; as, an anarthrous substantive. 2. (Zoöl.) Without joints, or having the joints indistinct, as some insects.
andranatomy: The dissection of a human body, especially of a male; androtomy. Coxe.
analyzation: The act of analyzing, or separating into constituent parts; analysis.
annulation: A circular or ringlike formation; a ring or belt. Nicholson.
antrustion: A vassal or voluntary follower of Frankish princes in their enterprises.
anfractuous: Winding; full of windings and turnings; sinuous; tortuous; as, the anfractuous spires of a born. -- An*frac"tu*ous*ness, n.
animalcular: Of, pertaining to, or resembling, animalcules. "Animalcular life." Tyndall.
anchoress: A female anchoret. And there, a saintly anchoress, she dwelt. Wordsworth.
aneroid: Containing no liquid; -- said of kind of barometer. Aneroid barometer, a barometer the action of which depends on the varying pressure of the atmosphere upon the elastic top of a metallic box (shaped like a watch) from which the air has been exhausted. An index shows the variation of pressure.
anglicize: To make English; to English; to anglify; render conformable to the English idiom, or to English analogies.
anaphora: A repetition of a word or of words at the beginning of two or more successive clauses.
antagonistic: Opposing in combat, combating; contending or acting against; as, antagonistic forces. -- An*tag`o*nis"tic*al*ly, adv. They were distinct, adverse, even antagonistic. Milman.
anisol: Methyl phenyl ether, C6H5OCH3, got by distilling anisic acid or by the action of methide on potassium phenolate.
anthobian: A beetle which feeds on flowers.
anion: An electro-negative element, or the element which, in electro- chemical decompositions, is evolved at the anode; -- opposed to cation. Faraday.
anaseismic: Moving up and down; -- said of earthquake shocks.
antisocial: Tending to interrupt or destroy social intercourse; averse to society, or hostile to its existence; as, antisocial principles.
answerable: 1. Obliged to answer; liable to be called to account; liable to pay, indemnify, or make good; accountable; amenable; responsible; as, an agent is answerable to his principal; to be answerable for a debt, or for damages. Will any man argue that . . . he can not be justly punished, but is answerable only to God Swift. 2. Capable of being answered or refuted;
anosmia: Loss of the sense of smell.
anseres: A Linnæan order of aquatic birds swimming by means of webbed feet, as the duck, or of lobed feet, as the grebe. In this order were included the geese, ducks, auks, divers, gulls, petrels, etc.
anorexy: Want of appetite, without a loathing of food. Coxe.
antistrophon: An argument retorted on an opponent. Milton.
angriness: The quality of being angry, or of being inclined to anger. Such an angriness of humor that we take fire at everything. Whole Duty of Man.
anatine: Of or pertaining to the ducks; ducklike.
antiloimic: A remedy against the plague. Brande & C.
anacrotism: A secondary notch in the pulse curve, obtained in a sphygmographic tracing.
anaglyptographic: Of or pertaining to anaglyptography; as, analyptographic engraving.
anecdotical: Pertaining to, consisting of, or addicted to, anecdotes. "Anecdotical traditions." Bolingbroke.
antique: 1. Old; ancient; of genuine antiquity; as, an antique statue. In this sense it usually refers to the flourishing ages of Greece and Rome. For the antique world excess and pride did hate. Spenser. 2. | In general, anything very old; but in a more limited sense, a relic or object of ancient art; collectively, the antique, the remains of ancient art, as busts, statues, paintings, and vases.
anamorphism: 1. A distorted image. 2. (Biol.) A gradual progression from one type to another, generally ascending. Huxley.
antigalastic: Causing a diminution or a suppression of the secretion of milk.
animate: 1. To give natural life to; to make alive; to quicken; as, the soul animates the body. 2. To give powers to, or to heighten the powers or effect of; as, to animate a lyre. Dryden. 3. | Endowed with life; alive; living; animated; lively. The admirable structure of animate bodies. Bentley.
animadversal: The faculty of perceiving; a percipient. (old) Dr. H. More.
anorthosite: A granular igneous rock composed almost exclusively of a soda- lime feldspar, usually labradorite.
anaglyphical: Pertaining to the art of chasing or embossing in relief; anaglyptic; -- opposed to diaglyptic or sunk work.
ansa: A name given to either of the projecting ends of Saturn's ring.
anticor: A dangerous inflammatory swelling of a horse's breast, just opposite the heart.
annuitant: One who receives, or its entitled to receive, an annuity. Lamb.
annulose: 1. Furnished with, or composed of, rings or ringlike segments; ringed. 2. (Zoöl.) Of or pertaining to the Annulosa.
annulata: A class of articulate animals, nearly equivalent to Annelida, including the marine annelids, earthworms, Gephyrea, Gymnotoma, leeches, etc. See Annelida.
antipapal: Opposed to the pope or to popery. Milton.
antarctic: Opposite to the northern or arctic pole; relating to the southern pole or to the region near it, and applied especially to a circle, distant from the pole 23º 28min. Thus we say the antarctic pole, circle, ocean, region, current, etc.
antaphrodisiac: Capable of blunting the venereal appetite. -- n. Anything that quells the venereal appetite.
angola: A fabric made from the wool of the Angora goat.
anacharis: A fresh-water weed of the frog's-bit family (Hydrocharidaceæ), native to America. Transferred to England it became an obstruction to navigation. Called also waterweed and water thyme.
anticlimax: A sentence in which the ideas fall, or become less important and striking, at the close; -- the opposite of climax. It produces a ridiculous effect. Example: Next comes Dalhousie, the great god of war, Lieutenant-colonel to the Earl ANTICLINAL An`ti*cli"nal, a. Etym: [Pref. anti- + Gr. Inclining or dipping in opposite directions. See Synclinal.
anthropotomist: One who is versed in anthropotomy, or human anatomy.
anticipant: Anticipating; expectant; -- with of. Wakening guilt, anticipant of hell. Southey.
anxiously: In an anxious manner; with painful uncertainty; solicitously.
angiosporous: Having spores contained in cells or thecæ, as in the case of some fungi.
antidromous: Changing the direction in the spiral sequence of leaves on a stem.
annoying: That annoys; molesting; vexatious. -- An*noy"ing*ly, adv.
anastatic: Pertaining to a process or a style of printing from characters in relief on zinc plates. Note: In this process the letterpress, engraving, or design of any kind is transferred to a zinc plate; the parts not covered with ink are eaten out, leaving a facsimile in relief to be printed from.
anabaptist: A name sometimes applied to a member of any sect holding that rebaptism is necessary for those baptized in infancy. Note: In church history, the name Anabaptists usually designates a sect of fanatics who greatly disturbed the peace of Germany, the Netherlands, etc., in the Reformation period.
anelectrotonus: The condition of decreased irritability of a nerve in the region of the positive electrode or anode on the passage of a current of electricity through it. Foster.
anthropopathism: The ascription of human feelings or passions to God, or to a polytheistic deity. In its recoil from the gross anthropopathy of the vulgar notions, it falls into the vacuum of absolute apathy. Hare.
antimonarchic: Opposed to monarchial government. Bp. Benson. Addison.
antitypy: Opposition or resistance of matter to force. Sir W. Hamilton.
anoxaemia: An abnormal condition due to deficient aëration of the blood, as in balloon sickness, mountain sickness. -- An`ox*æ"mic, *e"mic (#), a.
anthobranchia: A division of nudibranchiate Mollusca, in which the gills form a wreath or cluster upon the posterior part of the back. See Nudibranchiata, and Doris.
anxietude: The state of being anxious; anxiety.
antennule: A small antenna; -- applied to the smaller pair of antennæ or feelers of Crustacea.
anacoenosis: A figure by which a speaker appeals to his hearers or opponents for their opinion on the point in debate. Walker.
anthropocentric: Assuming man as the center or ultimate end; -- applied to theories of the universe or of any part of it, as the solar system. Draper.
anopsia: Want or defect of sight; blindness.
anglosaxondom: The Anglo-Saxon domain (i. e., Great Britain and the United States, etc.); the Anglo-Saxon race.
anacreontic: Pertaining to, after the manner of, or in the meter of, the Greek poet Anacreon; amatory and convivial. De Quincey. | A poem after the manner of Anacreon; a sprightly little poem in praise of love and wine.
anthokyan: The blue coloring matter of certain flowers. Same as Cyanin.
anomia: A genus of bivalve shells, allied to the oyster, so called from their unequal valves, of which the lower is perforated for attachment.
anomaly: 1. Deviation from the common rule; an irregularity; anything anomalous. We are enabled to unite into a consistent whole the various anomalies and contending principles that are found in the minds and affairs of men. Burke. As Professor Owen has remarked, there is no greater anomaly in nature than a bird that can not fly. Darwin. 2.
anthropogeny: The science or study of human generation, or the origin and development of man.
andron: The apartment appropriated for the males. This was in the lower part of the house.
antiphrasis: The use of words in a sense opposite to their proper meaning; as when a court of justice is called a court of vengeance.
ancile: The sacred shield of the Romans, said to have-fallen from heaven in the reign of Numa. It was the palladium of Rome.
antilogarithm: The number corresponding to a logarithm. The word has been sometimes, though rarely, used to denote the complement of a given logarithm; also the logarithmic cosine corresponding to a given logarithmic sine. -- An`ti*log`a*rith"mic, a.
antislavery: Opposed to slavery. -- n. Opposition to slavery.
andante: Moving moderately slow, but distinct and flowing; quicker than larghetto, and slower than allegretto. -- n. A movement or piece in andante time.
antiimperialism: Opposition to imperialism; -- applied specif., in the United States, after the Spanish-American war (1898), to the attitude or principles of those opposing territorial expansion; in England, of those, often called Little Englanders, opposing the extension of the empire and the closer relation of its parts, esp. in matters of commerce and imperial defense.
antiae: The two projecting feathered angles of the forehead of some birds; the frontal points.
annulosa: A division of the Invertebrata, nearly equivalent to the Articulata. It includes the Arthoropoda and Anarthropoda. By some zoölogists it is applied to the former only.
antacid: A remedy for acidity of the stomach, as an alkali or absorbent. -- a. Counteractive of acidity.
anchoretic: Pertaining to an anchoret or hermit; after the manner of an anchoret.
antemosaic: Being before the time of Moses.
anarchism: The doctrine or practice of anarchists.
antiquist: An antiquary; a collector of antiques. Pinkerton.
anon: 1. Straightway; at once. (old) The same is he that heareth the word, and anon with joy receiveth it. Matt. xiii. 20. 2. Soon; in a little while. As it shall better appear anon. Stow. 3. At another time; then; again. Sometimes he trots, . . . anon he rears upright. Shak. Anon right, at once; right off. (old) Chaucer. -- Ever and anon, now and then; frequently; often.
anemorphilous: Fertilized by the agency of the wind; -- said of plants in which the pollen is carried to the stigma by the wind; wind- Fertilized. Lubbock.
anthropotomical: Pertaining to anthropotomy, or the dissection of human bodies.
antiseptical: Counteracting or preventing putrefaction, or a putrescent tendency in the system; antiputrefactive. Antiseptic surgery, that system of surgical practice which insists upon a systematic use of antiseptics in the performance of operations and the dressing of wounds.
anachronistic: Erroneous in date; containing an anachronism. T. Warton.
anachronical: Characterized by, or involving, anachronism; anachronistic.
angerly: Angrily. [Obs. or Poetic] Why, how now, Hecate! you look angerly. Shak.
antiphone: The response which one side of the choir makes to the other in a chant; alternate chanting or signing.
and: 1. A particle which expresses the relation of connection or addition. It is used to conjoin a word with a word, a clause with a clause, or a sentence with a sentence. Note: (a) It is sometimes used emphatically; as, "there are women and women," that is, two very different sorts of women.
antibrachial: Of or pertaining to the antibrachium, or forearm.
antithetic: Pertaining to antithesis, or opposition of words and sentiments; containing, or of the nature of, antithesis; contrasted.
andalusite: A silicate of aluminium, occurring usually in thick rhombic prisms, nearly square, of a grayish or pale reddish tint. It was first discovered in Andalusia, Spain.
ano: A black bird of tropical America, the West Indies and Florida (Crotophaga ani), allied to the cuckoos, and remarkable for communistic nesting.
anlaut: An initial sound, as of a word or syllable. -- Im anlaut, initially; when initial; --used of sounds.
ankh: A tau cross with a loop at the top, used as an attribute or sacred emblem, symbolizing generation or enduring life. Called also crux ansata.
anemosis: A condition in the wood of some trees in which the rings are separated, as some suppose, by the action of high winds upon the trunk; wind shake.
anus: The posterior opening of the alimentary canal, through which the excrements are expelled.
antipodes: 1. Those who live on the side of the globe diametrically opposite. 2. The country of those who live on the opposite side of the globe. Latham. 3. Anything exactly opposite or contrary. Can there be a greater contrariety unto Christ's judgment, a more perfect antipodes to all that hath hitherto been gospel Hammond.
antlion: A neuropterous insect, the larva of which makes in the sand a pitfall to capture ants, etc. The common American species is Myrmeleon obsoletus, the European is M. formicarius.
antacrid: Corrective of acrimony of the humors.
anaclastics: That part of optics which treats of the refraction of light; -- commonly called dioptrics. Encyc. Brit.
anagogic: Mystical; having a secondary spiritual meaning; as, the rest of the Sabbath, in an anagogical sense, signifies the repose of the saints in heaven; an anagogical explication. -- An`a*gog"ic*al*ly, adv.
antiphlogistic: 1. (Chem.) Opposed to the doctrine of phlogiston. 2. (Med.) Counteracting inflammation. | Any medicine or diet which tends to check inflammation. Coxe.
angelical: Belonging to, or proceeding from, angels; resembling, characteristic of, or partaking of the nature of, an angel; heavenly; divine. "Angelic harps." Thomson."Angelical actions." Hooker. The union of womanly tenderness and angelic patience. Macaulay. Angelic Hymn, a very ancient hymn of the Christian Church;
antitheism: The doctrine of antitheists. -- An`ti*the*is"tic, a.
anlace: A broad dagger formerly worn at the girdle. [Written also anelace.]
anona: A genus of tropical or subtropical plants of the natural order Anonaceæ, including the soursop.
antimetabole: A figure in which the same words or ideas are repeated in transposed order.
anxiousness: The quality of being anxious; great solicitude; anxiety.
analogic: Of or belonging to analogy. Geo. Eliot.
anticness: The quality of being antic. Ford.
anathematical: Pertaining to, or having the nature of, an anathema. -- A*nath`e*mat"ic*al*ly, adv.
anastomosis: The inosculation of vessels, or intercommunication between two or more vessels or nerves, as the cross communication between arteries or veins.
antispastic: (a) Believed to cause a revulsion of fluids or of humors from one part to another. (old) (b) Counteracting spasms; antispasmodic. -- n. An antispastic agent.
antiodontalgic: Efficacious in curing toothache. -- n. A remedy for toothache.
anticlinorium: The upward elevation of the crust of the earth, resulting from a geanticlinal.
anthropophagy: The eating of human flesh; cannibalism.
anconeal: Of or pertaining to the ancon or elbow. "The olecranon on anconeal process." Flower.
anamorphosis: 1. (Persp.) A distorted or monstrous projection or representation of an image on a plane or curved surface, which, when viewed from a certain point, or as reflected from a curved mirror or through a polyhedron, appears regular and in proportion; a deformation of an image. 2. (Biol.) Same as Anamorphism, 2. 3.
anatifa: An animal of the barnacle tribe, of the genus Lepas, having a fleshy stem or peduncle; a goose barnacle. See Cirripedia. Note: The term Anatifæ, in the plural, is often used for the whole group of pedunculated cirripeds.
angioscope: An instrument for examining the capillary vessels of animals and plants. Morin.
anaerobic: Relating to, or like, anaërobies; araërobiotic.
anomy: Disregard or violation of law. Glanvill.
anchorlight: The lantern shown at night by a vessel at anchor. International rules of the road require vessels at anchor to carry from sunset to sunrise a single white light forward if under 150 feet in length, and if longer, two such lights, one near the stern and one forward.
anagrammatize: To transpose, as the letters of a word, so as to form an anagram. Cudworth.
anabaptistical: Relating or attributed to the Anabaptists, or their doctrines. Milton. Bp. Bull.
annuity: A sum of money, payable yearly, to continue for a given number of years, for life, or forever; an annual allowance.
ancientry: 1. Antiquity; what is ancient. They contain not word of ancientry. West. 2. Old age; also, old people. Wronging the ancientry. Shak. 3. Ancient lineage; ancestry; dignity of birth. A gentleman of more ancientry than estate. Fuller.
angularly: In an angular manner; with of at angles or corners. B. Jonson.
anubis: An Egyptian deity, the conductor of departed spirits, represented by a human figure with the head of a dog or fox.
anilide: One of a class of compounds which may be regarded as amides in which more or less of the hydrogen has been replaced by phenyl.
analytic: Of or pertaining to analysis; resolving into elements or constituent parts; as, an analytical experiment; analytic reasoning; -- opposed to synthetic. Analytical or coördinate geometry. See under Geometry. -- Analytic language, a noninflectional language or one not characterized by grammatical endings. -- Analytical table (Nat.
anagogical: Mystical; having a secondary spiritual meaning; as, the rest of the Sabbath, in an anagogical sense, signifies the repose of the saints in heaven; an anagogical explication. -- An`a*gog"ic*al*ly, adv.
androtomous: Having the filaments of the stamens divided into two parts.
ant: A hymenopterous insect of the Linnæan genus Formica, which is now made a family of several genera; an emmet; a pismire. Note: Among ants, as among bees, there are neuter or working ants, besides the males and females; the former are without wings.
analysis: 1. A resolution of anything, whether an object of the senses or of the intellect, into its constituent or original elements; an examination of the component parts of a subject, each separately, as the words which compose a sentence, the tones of a tune, or the simple propositions which enter into an argument. It is opposed to synthesis. 2.
anathematic: Pertaining to, or having the nature of, an anathema. -- A*nath`e*mat"ic*al*ly, adv.
antonomasia: The use of some epithet or the name of some office, dignity, or the like, instead of the proper name of the person; as when his majesty is used for a king, or when, instead of Aristotle, we say, the philosopher; or, conversely, the use of a proper name instead of an appellative, as when a wise man is called a Solomon, or an eminent orator a Cicero.
angulosity: A state of being angulous or angular. (old)
analogist: One who reasons from analogy, or represent, by analogy. Cheyne.
anoetic: 1. Unthinkable. [Rare] 2. (Psychol.) Not subject to conscious attention; having an indefinite, relatively passive, conscious being; characteristic of the "fringe" or "margin" of consciousness. Presentation considered as having an existence relatively independent of thought, may be called sentience, or anoetic consciousness.
anxious: 1. Full of anxiety or disquietude; greatly concerned or solicitous, esp. respecting future or unknown; being in painful suspense; -- applied to persons; as, anxious for the issue of a battle. 2. Accompanied with, or causing, anxiety; worrying; -- applied to things; as, anxious labor. The sweet of life, from which God hath bid dwell far off all anxious cares. Milton. 3.
antechoir: (a) A space inclosed or reserved at the entrance to the choir, for the clergy and choristers. (b) Where a choir is divided, as in some Spanish churches, that division of it which is the farther from the sanctuary.
antiphon: 1. A musical response; alternate singing or chanting. See Antiphony, and Antiphone. 2. A verse said before and after the psalms. Shipley.
antediluvian: Of or relating to the period before the Deluge in Noah's time; hence, antiquated; as, an antediluvian vehicle. -- n. One who lived before the Deluge.
angor: Great anxiety accompanied by painful constriction at the upper part of the belly, often with palpitation and oppression.
anthropomorphology: The application to God of terms descriptive of human beings.
antcow: Any aphid from which ants obtain honeydew.
anglesite: A native sulphate of lead. It occurs in white or yellowish transparent, prismatic crystals.
angelhood: The state of being an angel; angelic nature. Mrs. Browning.
analogous: Having analogy; corresponding to something else; bearing some resemblance or proportion; -- often followed by to. Analogous tendencies in arts and manners. De Quincey. Decay of public spirit, which may be considered analogous to natural death. J. H. Newman. nalogous pole (Pyroelect.), that pole of a crystal which becomes positively electrified when heated. Syn.
anyhow: In any way or manner whatever; at any rate; in any event. Anyhow, it must be acknowledged to be not a simple selforiginated error. J. H. Newman. Anyhow, the languages of the two nations were closely allied. E. A. Freeman.
annotator: A writer of annotations; a commentator.
antipyrine: An artificial alkaloid, believed to be efficient in abating fever.
animus: Animating spirit; intention; temper. nimus furandi Etym: [L.] (Law), intention of stealing.
antinephritic: Counteracting, or deemed of use in, diseases of the kidneys. -- n. An antinephritic remedy.
annunciator: 1. One who announces. Specifically: An officer in the church of Constantinople, whose business it was to inform the people of the festivals to be celebrated. 2. An indicator (as in a hotel) which designates the room where attendance is wanted.
anteport: An outer port, gate, or door.
anteriority: The state of being anterior or preceding in time or in situation; priority. Pope.
anemoscope: An instrument which shows the direction of the wind; a wind vane; a weathercock; -- usually applied to a contrivance consisting of a vane above, connected in the building with a dial or index with pointers to show the changes of the wind.
antiscii: The inhabitants of the earth, living on different sides of the equator, whose shadows at noon are cast in opposite directions. The inhabitants of the north and south temperate zones are always Antiscians. Brande & C.
ancillary: Subservient or subordinate, like a handmaid; auxiliary. The Convocation of York seems to have been always considered as inferior, and even ancillary, to the greater province. Hallam.
androecium: The stamens of a flower taken collectively.
antimacassar: A cover for the back or arms of a chair or sofa, etc., to prevent them from being soiled by macassar or other oil from the hair.
antimonate: A compound of antimonic acid with a base or basic radical. [Written also antimoniate.]
antlia: The spiral tubular proboscis of lepidopterous insects. See Lepidoptera.
antipodean: Pertaining to the antipodes, or the opposite side of the world; antipodal.
annotatory: Pertaining to an annotator; containing annotations.
anenterous: Destitute of a stomach or an intestine. Owen.
anglice: In English; in the English manner; as, Livorno, Anglice Leghorn.
anodon: A genus of fresh-water bivalves, having to teeth at the hinge. [Written also Anodonta.]
anarch: The author of anarchy; one who excites revolt. Milton. Imperial anarchs doubling human woes. Byron.
anconeus: A muscle of the elbow and forearm.
antagonism: Opposition of action; counteraction or contrariety of things or principles. Note: We speak of antagonism between two things, to or against a thing, and sometimes with a thing.
anaglyptics: The art of carving in low relief, embossing, etc.
anadromous: 1. (Zoöl.) Ascending rivers from the sea, at certain seasons, for breeding, as the salmon, shad, etc. 2. (Bot.) Tending upwards; -- said of terns in which the lowest secondary segments are on the upper side of the branch of the central stem. D. C. Eaton.
antidysenteric: Good against dysentery. -- n. A medicine for dysentery.
anacathartic: Producing vomiting or expectoration. -- n. An anacatharic medicine; an expectorant or an emetic.
antherozooid: One of the mobile male reproductive bodies in the antheridia of cryptogams.
antimere: One of the two halves of bilaterally symmetrical animals; one of any opposite symmetrical or homotypic parts in animals and plants.
anthropopathical: Of or pertaining to anthropopathy. -- An`thro*po*path"ic*al*ly, adv. The daring anthropopathic imagery by which the prophets often represent God as chiding, upbraiding, threatening. H. Rogers.
antecedence: 1. The act or state of going before in time; precedence. H. Spenser. 2. (Astron.) An apparent motion of a planet toward the west; retrogradation.
antefix: (a) An ornament fixed upon a frieze. (b) An ornament at the eaves, concealing the ends of the joint tiles of the roof. (c) An ornament of the cymatium of a classic cornice, sometimes pierced for the escape of water.
anatreptic: Overthrowing; defeating; -- applied to Plato's refutative dialogues. Enfield.
angulated: Having angles or corners; angled; as, angulate leaves.
androides: A machine or automaton in the form of a human being.
anathema: 1. A ban or curse pronounced with religious solemnity by ecclesiastical authority, and accompanied by excommunication. Hence: Denunciation of anything as accursed. [They] denounce anathemas against unbelievers. Priestley. 2. An imprecation; a curse; a malediction. Finally she fled to London followed by the anathemas of both [families]. Thackeray. 3.
anolis: A genus of lizards which belong to the family Iguanidæ. They take the place in the New World of the chameleons in the Old, and in America are often called chameleons.
android: A machine or automaton in the form of a human being.
anthozoan: Pertaining to the Anthozoa. -- n. One of the Anthozoa.
anthological: Pertaining to anthology; consisting of beautiful extracts from different authors, especially the poets. He published a geographical and anthological description of all empires and kingdoms . . . in this terrestrial globe. Wood.
anime: Of a different tincture from the animal itself; -- said of the eyes of a rapacious animal. Brande & C. | A resin exuding from a tropical American tree (Hymenæa courbaril), and much used by varnish makers. Ure.
angiocarpous: (a) Having fruit inclosed within a covering that does not form a part of itself; as, the filbert covered by its husk, or the acorn seated in its cupule. Brande & C. (b) Having the seeds or spores covered, as in certain lichens. Gray.
antrorse: Forward or upward in direction. Gray.
anti: A prefix meaning against, opposite or opposed to, contrary, or in place of; -- used in composition in many English words. It is often shortened to ant-; as, antacid, antarctic.
annelidan: Of or pertaining to the Annelida. -- n. One of the Annelida.
antidotary: Antidotal. -- n. Antidote; also, a book of antidotes.
analyze: To subject to analysis; to resolve (anything complex) into its elements; to separate into the constituent parts, for the purpose of an examination of each separately; to examine in such a manner as to ascertain the elements or nature of the thing examined; as, to analyze a fossil substance; to analyze a sentence or a word; to analyze an action to ascertain its morality.
analogy: 1. A resemblance of relations; an agreement or likeness between things in some circumstances or effects, when the things are otherwise entirely different. Thus, learning enlightens the mind, because it is to the mind what light is to the eye, enabling it to discover things before hidden. Note: Followed by between, to, or with;
ankled: Having ankles; -- used in composition; as, well-ankled. Beau. & Fl.
angioma: A tumor composed chiefly of dilated blood vessels.
animose: Full of spirit; hot; vehement; resolute. (old) Ash.
anglemeter: An instrument to measure angles, esp. one used by geologists to measure the dip of strata.
anopsy: Want or defect of sight; blindness.
anthracometer: An instrument for measuring the amount of carbonic acid in a mixture.
anticipation: 1. The act of anticipating, taking up, placing, or considering something beforehand, or before the proper time in natural order. So shall my anticipation prevent your discovery. Shak. 2. Previous view or impression of what is to happen; instinctive prevision; foretaste; antepast; as, the anticipation of the joys of heaven.
angariation: Exaction of forced service; compulsion. (old) Speed.
anfractuosity: 1. A state of being anfractuous, or full of windings and turnings; sinuosity. The anfractuosities of his intellect and temper. Macaulay. 2. (Anat.) A sinuous depression or sulcus like those separating the convolutions of the brain.
anelectric: Not becoming electrified by friction; -- opposed to idioelectric. -- n. A substance incapable of being electrified by friction. Faraday.
anabasis: 1. A journey or expedition up from the coast, like that of the younger Cyrus into Central Asia, described by Xenophon in his work called "The Anabasis." The anabasis of Napoleon. De Quincey. 2. (Med.) The first period, or increase, of a disease; augmentation. (old)
anthophagous: Eating flowers; -- said of certain insects.
analeptic: Restorative; giving strength after disease. -- n. A restorative.
ani: A black bird of tropical America, the West Indies and Florida (Crotophaga ani), allied to the cuckoos, and remarkable for communistic nesting.
anticyclone: A movement of the atmosphere opposite in character, as regards direction of the wind and distribution of barometric pressure, to that of a cyclone. -- An`ti*cy*clon"ic, a. -- An`ti*cy*clon"ic*al*ly, adv.
annihilator: One who, or that which, annihilates; as, a fire annihilator.
analogue: 1. That which is analogous to, or corresponds with, some other thing. The vexatious tyranny of the individual despot meets its analogue in the insolent tyranny of the many. I. Taylor. 2. (Philol.) A word in one language corresponding with one in another; an analogous term; as, the Latin "pater" is the analogue of the English "father." 3. (Nat.
anteroom: A room before, or forming an entrance to, another; a waiting room.
annicut: A dam or mole made in the course of a stream for the purpose of regulating the flow of a system of irrigation. [India] Brande & C.
antisyphilitic: Efficacious against syphilis. -- n. A medicine for syphilis.
annotate: To explain or criticize by notes; as, to annotate the works of Bacon. | To make notes or comments; -- with on or upon.
anthropomorphic: Of or pertaining to anthromorphism. Hadley. -- An`thro*po*mor"phic*al*ly, adv.
antisplenetic: Good as a remedy against disease of the spleen. -- n. An antisplenetic medicine.
annular: 1. Pertaining to, or having the form of, a ring; forming a ring; ringed; ring-shaped; as, annular fibers. 2. Banded or marked with circles. Annular eclipse (Astron.), an eclipse of the sun in which the moon at the middle of the eclipse conceals the central part of the sun's disk, leaving a complete ring of light around the border.
anele: 1. To anoint. Shipley. 2. To give extreme unction to. (old) R. of Brunne.
androgyne: 1. An hermaphrodite. 2. (Bot.) An androgynous plant. Whewell.
anthropologic: Pertaining to anthropology; belonging to the nature of man. "Anthropologic wisdom." Kingsley. -- An`thro*po*log"ic*al*ly, adv.
anhistous: Without definite structure; as, an anhistous membrane.
anight: In the night time; at night. (old) Does he hawk anights still Marston.
androcephalous: Having a human head (upon an animal's body), as the Egyptian sphinx.
anglican: 1. English; of or pertaining to England or the English nation; especially, pertaining to, or connected with, the established church of England; as, the Anglican church, doctrine, orders, ritual, etc. | 1. A member of the Church of England. Whether Catholics, Anglicans, or Calvinists. Burke. 2. In a restricted sense, a member of the High Church party, or of the more advanced ritualistic section, in…
answerableness: The quality of being answerable, liable, responsible, or correspondent.
anatomic: Of or relating to anatomy or dissection; as, the anatomic art; anatomical observations. Hume.
anaptychus: One of a pair of shelly plates found in some cephalopods, as the ammonites.
antiphonary: A book containing a collection of antiphons; the book in which the antiphons of the breviary, with their musical notes, are contained.
antiphthisic: Relieving or curing phthisis, or consumption. -- n. A medicine for phthisis.
antibromic: An agent that destroys offensive smells; a deodorizer.
anthracic: Of or relating to anthrax; as, anthracic blood.
antistrumatic: Antistrumous. -- n. A medicine for scrofula.
antelope: One of a group of ruminant quadrupeds, intermediate between the deer and the goat. The horns are usually annulated, or ringed. There are many species in Africa and Asia. The antelope and wolf both fierce and fell. Spenser. Note: The common or bezoar antelope of India is Antilope bezoartica. The chamois of the Alps, the gazelle, the addax, and the eland are other species.
anaerobes: Anaërobic bacteria. They are called facultative anaërobia when able to live either in the presence or absence of free oxygen; obligate, or obligatory, anaërobia when they thrive only in its absence.
antler: The entire horn, or any branch of the horn, of a cervine animal, as of a stag. Huge stags with sixteen antlers. Macaulay. Note: The branch next to the head is called the brow antler, and the branch next above, the bez antler, or bay antler. The main stem is the beam, and the branches are often called tynes.
anthropolite: A petrifaction of the human body, or of any portion of it.
annalistic: Pertaining to, or after the manner of, an annalist; as, the dry annalistic style."A stiff annalistic method." Sir G. C. Lewis.
anomalism: An anomaly; a deviation from rule. Hooker.
anticoherer: A device, one form of which consists of a scratched deposit of silver on glass, used in connection with the receiving apparatus for reading wireless signals. The electric waves falling on this contrivance increase its resistance several times. The anticoherer can be used in conjunction with a telephone.
anoa: A small wild ox of Celebes (Anoa depressicornis), allied to the buffalo, but having long nearly straight horns.
annats: The first year's profits of a spiritual preferment, anciently paid by the clergy to the pope; first fruits. In England, they now form a fund for the augmentation of poor livings.
antipodal: 1. Pertaining to the antipodes; situated on the opposite side of the globe. 2. Diametrically opposite. His antipodal shadow." Lowell.
angles: An ancient Low German tribe, that settled in Britain, which came to be called Engla-land (Angleland or England). The Angles probably came from the district of Angeln (now within the limits of Schleswig), and the country now Lower Hanover, etc.
anthropoglot: An animal which has a tongue resembling that of man, as the parrot.
anacoluthon: A want of grammatical sequence or coherence in a sentence; an instance of a change of construction in a sentence so that the latter part does not syntactically correspond with the first part.
anchovypear: A West Indian fruit like the mango in taste, sometimes pickled; also, the tree (Grias cauliflora) bearing this fruit.
anisette: A French cordial or liqueur flavored with anise seeds. De Colange.
anecdote: 1. pl. Unpublished narratives. Burke. 2. A particular or detached incident or fact of an interesting nature; a biographical incident or fragment; a single passage of private life.
anasarca: Dropsy of the subcutaneous cellular tissue; an effusion of serum into the cellular substance, occasioning a soft, pale, inelastic swelling of the skin.
antenuptial: Preceding marriage; as, an antenuptial agreement. Kent.
anacardiaceous: Belonging to, or resembling, a family, or order, of plants of which the cashew tree is the type, and the species of sumac are well known examples.
analogically: In an analogical sense; in accordance with analogy; by way of similitude. A prince is analogically styled a pilot, being to the state as a pilot is to the vessel. Berkeley.
antiperistasis: Opposition by which the quality opposed asquires strength; resistance or reaction roused by opposition or by the action of an opposite principle or quality.
anencephalous: Without a brain; brainless. Todd & B.
antepileptic: Good against epilepsy. -- n. A medicine for epilepsy.
annualist: One who writes for, or who edits, an annual.
anisodactyla: (a) A group of herbivorous mammals characterized by having the hoofs in a single series around the foot, as the elephant, rhinoceros, etc. (b) A group of perching birds which are anisodactylous.
antidotal: Having the quality an antidote; fitted to counteract the effects of poison. Sir T. Browne. -- An"ti*do`tal*ly, adv.
antiar: A Virulent poison prepared in Java from the gum resin of one species of the upas tree (Antiaris toxicaria).
antipathist: One who has an antipathy. "Antipathist of light." Coleridge.
antiphony: 1. A musical response; also, antiphonal chanting or signing. 2. An anthem or psalm sung alternately by a choir or congregation divided into two parts. Also figuratively. O! never more for me shall winds intone, With all your tops, a vast antiphony. R. Browning.
annunciatory: Pertaining to, or containing, announcement; making known.
anastomose: To inosculate; to intercommunicate by anastomosis, as the arteries and veins. The ribbing of the leaf, and the anastomosing network of its vessels. I. Taylor.
antipode: One of the antipodes; anything exactly opposite. In tale or history your beggar is ever the just antipode to your king. Lamb. Note: The singular, antipode, is exceptional in formation, but has been used by good writers. Its regular English plural would be ân"tî*podes, the last syllable rhyming with abodes, and this pronunciation is sometimes heard.
ancestry: 1. Condition as to ancestors; ancestral lineage; hence, birth or honorable descent. Title and ancestry render a good man more illustrious, but an ill one more contemptible. Addison. 2. A series of ancestors or progenitors; lineage, or those who compose the line of natural descent.
anury: Nonsecretion or defective secretion of urine; ischury.
antiquarianize: To act the part of an antiquary. [Colloq.]
antisocialist: One opposed to the doctrines and practices of socialists or socialism.
anthracite: A hard, compact variety of mineral coal, of high luster, differing from bituminous coal in containing little or no bitumen, in consequence of which it burns with a nearly non luminous flame. The purer specimens consist almost wholly of carbon. Also called glance coal and blind coal.
anoplura: A group of insects which includes the lice.
androgynism: Union of both sexes in one individual; hermaphroditism.
analectic: Relating to analects; made up of selections; as, an analectic magazine.
antitoxine: A substance (sometimes the product of a specific micro-organism and sometimes naturally present in the blood or tissues of an animal), capable of producing immunity from certain diseases, or of counteracting the poisonous effects of pathogenic bacteria.
antiarin: A poisonous principle obtained from antiar. Watts.
anthropomorphite: One who ascribes a human form or human attributes to the Deity or to a polytheistic deity. Taylor. Specifically, one of a sect of ancient heretics who believed that God has a human form, etc. Tillotson.
angelify: To make like an angel; to angelize. (old) Farindon (1647).
anagoge: 1. An elevation of mind to things celestial. 2. The spiritual meaning or application; esp. the application of the types and allegories of the Old Testament to subjects of the New.
anallantoidea: The division of Vertebrata in which no allantois is developed. It includes amphibians, fishes, and lower forms.
anatomist: One who is skilled in the art of anatomy, or dissection.
anodyne: Serving to assuage pain; soothing. The anodyne draught of oblivion. Burke. Note: "The word [in a medical sense] in chiefly applied to the different preparations of opium, belladonna, hyoscyamus, and… | Any medicine which allays pain, as an opiate or narcotic; anything that soothes disturbed feelings.
ancone: (a) The corner or quoin of a wall, cross-beam, or rafter. (old) Gwilt. (b) A bracket supporting a cornice; a console.
angiology: That part of anatomy which treats of blood vessels and lymphatics.
anatiferous: Producing ducks; -- applied to Anatifæ, under the absurd notion of their turning into ducks or geese. See Barnacle.
anhinga: An aquatic bird of the southern United States (Platus anhinga); the darter, or snakebird.
anomoura: A group of decapod Crustacea, of which the hermit crab in an example.
antiattrition: Anything to prevent the effects of friction, esp. a compound lubricant for machinery, etc., often consisting of plumbago, with some greasy material; antifriction grease.
anteversion: A displacement of an organ, esp. of the uterus, in such manner that its whole axis is directed further forward than usual.
angiosperm: A plant which has its seeds inclosed in a pericarp. Note: The term is restricted to exogenous plants, and applied to one of the two grand divisions of these species, the other division including gymnosperms, or those which have naked seeds. The oak, apple, beech, etc., are angiosperms, while the pines, spruce, hemlock, and the allied varieties, are gymnosperms.
antemural: An outwork of a strong, high wall, with turrets, in front gateway (as of an old castle), for defending the entrance.
annealer: One who, or that which, anneals.
annoyance: 1. The act of annoying, or the state of being annoyed; molestation; vexation; annoy. A deep clay, giving much annoyance to passengers. Fuller. For the further annoyance and terror of any besieged place, they would throw into it dead bodies. Wilkins. 2. That which annoys. A grain, a dust, a gnat, a wandering hair, Any annoyance in that precious sense. Shak.
angrily: In an angry manner; under the influence of anger.
anatomism: 1. The application of the principles of anatomy, as in art. The stretched and vivid anatomism of their [i. e., the French] great figure painters. The London Spectator. 2. The doctrine that the anatomical structure explains all the phenomena of the organism or of animal life.
anisometropia: Unequal refractive power in the two eyes.
anasarcous: Belonging, or affected by, anasarca, or dropsy; dropsical. Wiseman.
anachorism: An error in regard to the place of an event or a thing; a referring something to a wrong place.
anthracnose: Any one of several fungus diseases, caused by parasitic species of the series Melanconiales, attacking the bean, grape, melon, cotton, and other plants. In the case of the grape, brown concave spots are formed on the stem and fruit, and the disease is called bird's-eye rot.
annunciable: That may be announced or declared; declarable.
anonymous: Nameless; of unknown name; also, of unknown /or unavowed authorship; as, an anonymous benefactor; an anonymous pamphlet or letter.
anker: A liquid measure in various countries of Europe. The Dutch anker, formerly also used in England, contained about 10 of the old wine gallons, or 8
anapest: 1. (Pros.) A metrical foot consisting of three syllables, the first two short, or unaccented, the last long, or accented; the reverse of the dactyl. In Latin d, and in English in-ter-vene, are examples of anapests. 2. A verse composed of such feet.
angle: 1. The inclosed space near the point where two lines; a corner; a nook. Into the utmost angle of the world. Spenser. To search the tenderest angles of the heart. Milton. 2. | 1. To fish with an angle (fishhook), or with hook and line. 2. To use some bait or artifice; to intrigue; to scheme; as, to angle for praise. The hearts of all that he did angle for. Shak.
anabatic: Pertaining to anabasis; as, an anabatic fever. (old)
antitype: That of which the type pattern or representation; that which is represented by the type or symbol.
anaerobiotic: Related to, or of the nature of, anaërobies.
anoplotherium: A genus of extinct quadrupeds of the order Ungulata, whose were first found in the gypsum quarries near Paris; characterized by the shortness and feebleness of their canine teeth (whence the name).
anisomerous: Having the number of floral organs unequal, as four petals and six stamens.
anarthropodous: Having no jointed legs; pertaining to Anarthropoda.
antipathous: Having a natural contrariety; adverse; antipathetic. (old) Beau. & Fl.
angelus: (a) A form of devotion in which three Ave Marias are repeated. It is said at morning, noon, and evening, at the sound of a bell. (b) The Angelus bell. Shipley.
announce: 1. To give public notice, or first notice of; to make known; to publish; to proclaim. Her [Q. Elizabeth's] arrival was announced through the country by a peal of cannon from the ramparts. Gilpin. 2. To pronounce; to declare by judicial sentence. Publish laws, announce Or life or death. Prior. Syn. -- To proclaim; publish; make known; herald; declare; promulgate.
angusticlave: A narrow stripe of purple worn by the equites on each side of the tunic as a sign of rank.
antichronical: Deviating from the proper order of time. -- An`ti*chron"ic*al*ly, adv.
anisyl: (a) The univalent radical, CH3OC6H4, of which anisol is the hydride. (b) The univalent radical CH3OC6H4CH2; as, anisyl alcohol. (c) The univalent radical CH3OC6H4CO, of anisic acid.
animating: Causing animation; life-giving; inspiriting; rousing. "Animating cries." Pope. -- An"i*ma`ting*ly, adv.
anisocoria: Inequality of the pupils of the eye.
anapestic: Pertaining to an anapest; consisting of an anapests; as, an anapestic meter, foot, verse. -- n. Anapestic measure or verse.
andromeda: 1. (Astron.) A northern constellation, supposed to represent the mythical Andromeda. 2. (bot.) A genus of ericaceous flowering plants of northern climates, of which the original species was found growing on a rock surrounded by water.
animalculism: The theory which seeks to explain certain physiological and pathological by means of animalcules.
ancestor: 1. One from whom a person is descended, whether on the father's or mother's side, at any distance of time; a progenitor; a fore father. 2. (Biol.) An earlier type; a progenitor; as, this fossil animal is regarded as the ancestor of the horse. 3. (Law) One from whom an estate has descended; -- the correlative of heir.
answerless: Having no answer, or impossible to be answered. Byron. AN 'T An 't. An it, that is, and it or if it. See An, conj. (old) AN'T An't. A contraction for are and am not; also used for is not; -- now usually written ain't. [Colloq. & illiterate speech.]
ancient: 1. Old; that happened or existed in former times, usually at a great distance of time; belonging to times long past; specifically applied to the times before the fall of the Roman empire; | 1. pl. Those who lived in former ages, as opposed to the moderns. 2. An aged man; a patriarch. Hence: A governor; a ruler; a person of influence. The Lord will enter into judgment with the ancients…
anotherguess: Of another sort. (old) It used to go in another-guess manner. Arbuthnot.
antimetathesis: An antithesis in which the members are repeated in inverse order.
anagogics: Mystical interpretations or studies, esp. of the Scriptures. L. Addison.
anomaliped: One of a group of perching birds, having the middle toe more or less united to the outer and inner ones.
antepaschal: Pertaining to the time before the Passover, or before Easter.
anthropopathite: One who ascribes human feelings to deity.
anakim: A race of giants living in Palestine.
annates: The first year's profits of a spiritual preferment, anciently paid by the clergy to the pope; first fruits. In England, they now form a fund for the augmentation of poor livings.
antistrumous: Good against scrofulous disorders. Johnson. Wiseman.
anteal: Being before, or in front. J. Fleming.
ancon: The olecranon, or the elbow. Ancon sheep (Zoöl.), a breed of sheep with short crooked legs and long back. It originated in Massachusetts in 1791; -- called also the otter breed. | (a) The corner or quoin of a wall, cross-beam, or rafter. (old) Gwilt. (b) A bracket supporting a cornice; a console.
antoecians: Those who live under the same meridian, but on opposite parallels of latitude, north and south of the equator.
anisometric: Not isometric; having unsymmetrical parts; -- said of crystals with three unequal axes. Dana.
animadvert: 1. To take notice; to observe; -- commonly followed by that. Dr. H. More. 2. To consider or remark by way of criticism or censure; to express censure; -- with on or upon. I should not animadvert on him . . . if he had not used extreme severity in his judgment of the incomparable Shakespeare. Dryden. 3. To take cognizance judicially; to inflict punishment. (old) Grew. Syn.
antivenin: The serum of blood rendered antitoxic to a venom by repeated injections of small doses of the venom.
antestature: A small intrenchment or work of palisades, or of sacks of earth.
antemetic: Tending to check vomiting. -- n. A remedy to check or allay vomiting.
anarchal: Lawless; anarchical. We are in the habit of calling those bodies of men anarchal which are in a state of effervescence. Landor.
anthophilous: Lit., fond of flowers; hence, feeding upon, or living among, flowers.
antimoniated: Combined or prepared with antimony; as, antimoniated tartar.
antisacerdotal: Hostile to priests or the priesthood. Waterland.
anaesthetize: To render insensible by an anæsthetic. Encyc. Brit.
androphore: 1. (Bot.) A support or column on which stamens are raised. Gray. 2. (Zoöl.) The part which in some Siphonophora bears the male gonophores.
anguish: Extreme pain, either of body or mind; excruciating distress. But they hearkened not unto Moses for anguish of spirit, and for cruel bondage. Ex. vi. 9. Anguish as of her that bringeth forth her first… | To distress with extreme pain or grief. Temple.
anthropography: That branch of anthropology which treats of the actual distribution of the human race in its different divisions, as distinguished by physical character, language, institutions, and customs, in contradistinction to ethnography, which treats historically of the origin and filiation of races and nations. P. Cyc.
antifriction: Something to lessea. Tending to lessen friction.
anteposition: The placing of a before another, which, by ordinary rules, ought to follow it.
angiospermous: Having seeds inclosed in a pod or other pericarp.
anadiplosis: A repetition of the last word or any prominent word in a sentence or clause, at the beginning of the next, with an adjunct idea; as, "He retained his virtues amidst all his misfortunes -- misfortunes which no prudence could foresee or prevent."
anchorshot: A shot made with the object balls in an anchor space.
anxiety: 1. Concern or solicitude respecting some thing o 2. Eager desire. J. D. Forbes 3. (Med.) A state of restlessness and agitation, often with general indisposition and a distressing sense of oppression at the epigastrium. Dunglison. Syn. -- Care; solicitude; foreboding; uneasiness; perplexity; disquietude; disquiet; trouble; apprehension; restlessness. See Care.
anythingarian: One who holds to no particular creed or dogma.
anthill: A mound thrown up by ants or by termites in forming their nests.
anteater: One of several species of edentates and monotremes that feed upon ants. See Ant-bear, Pangolin, Aard-vark, and Echidna.
antialbumid: A body formed from albumin by pancreatic and gastric digestion. It is convertible into antipeptone.
antechapel: The outer part of the west end of a collegiate or other chapel. Shipley.
antimeter: A modification of the quadrant, for measuring small angles. (old)
anglomania: A mania for, or an inordinate attachment to, English customs, institutions, etc.
antiorgastic: Tending to allay venereal excitement or desire; sedative.
antiseptic: Counteracting or preventing putrefaction, or a putrescent tendency in the system; antiputrefactive. Antiseptic surgery, that system of surgical practice which insists upon a systematic use of… | A substance which prevents or retards putrefaction, or destroys, or protects from, putrefactive organisms; as, salt, carbolic acid, alcohol, cinchona.
antiputrefactive: Counteracting, or preserving from, putrefaction; antiseptic.
animism: 1. The doctrine, taught by Stahl, that the soul is the proper principle of life and development in the body. 2. The belief that inanimate objects and the phenomena of nature are endowed with personal life or a living soul; also, in an extended sense, the belief in the existence of soul or spirit apart from matter. Tylor.
anarchic: Pertaining to anarchy; without rule or government; in political confusion; tending to produce anarchy; as, anarchic despotism; anarchical opinions.
animalculine: Of, pertaining to, or resembling, animalcules. "Animalcular life." Tyndall.
androspore: A spore of some algæ, which has male functions.
anise: 1. (Bot.) An umbelliferous plant (Pimpinella anisum) growing naturally in Egypt, and cultivated in Spain, Malta, etc., for its carminative and aromatic seeds. 2. The fruit or seeds of this plant.
anura: One of the orders of amphibians characterized by the absence of a tail, as the frogs and toads. [Written also anoura.]
annoy: A feeling of discomfort or vexation caused by what one dislikes; also, whatever causes such a feeling; as, to work annoy. Worse than Tantalus' is her annoy. Shak.
