anatomize: 1. To dissect; to cut in pieces, as an animal vegetable body, for the purpose of displaying or examining the structure and use of the several parts. 2. To discriminate minutely or carefully; to analyze. If we anatomize all other reasonings of this nature, we shall find that they are founded on the relation of cause and effect. Hume.
anode: The positive pole of an electric battery, or more strictly the electrode by which the current enters the electrolyte on its way to the other pole; -- opposed to cathode.
anticline: A structure of bedded rocks in which the beds on both sides of an axis or axial plane dip away from the axis; an anticlinal.
antimoniureted: Combined with or containing antimony; as, antimoniureted hydrogen. [Written also antimoniuretted.]
antiplastic: 1. Diminishing plasticity. 2. (Med.) Preventing or checking the process of healing, or granulation.
antenna: A movable, articulated organ of sensation, attached to the heads of insects and Crustacea. There are two in the former, and usually four in the latter. They are used as organs of touch, and in some species of Crustacea the cavity of the ear is situated near the basal joint. In insects, they are popularly called horns, and also feelers.
antemortem: Before death; -- generally used adjectivelly; as, an ante- mortem statement; ante-mortem examination. The ante-mortem statement, or dying declaration made in view of death, by one injured, as to the cause and manner of the injury, is often receivable in evidence against one charged with causing the death.
antagonistical: Opposing in combat, combating; contending or acting against; as, antagonistic forces. -- An*tag`o*nis"tic*al*ly, adv. They were distinct, adverse, even antagonistic. Milman.
anathematism: Anathematization. (old) We find a law of Justinian forbidding anathematisms to be pronounced against the Jewish Hellenists. J. Taylor.
angelot: 1. A French gold coin of the reign of Louis XI., bearing the image of St. Michael; also, a piece coined at Paris by the English under Henry VI. (old) 2. An instrument of music, of the lute kind, now disused. Johnson. R. Browning. 3. A sort of small, rich cheese, made in Normandy.
anatomical: Of or relating to anatomy or dissection; as, the anatomic art; anatomical observations. Hume.
analgen: A crystalline compound used as an antipyretic and analgesic, employed chiefly in rheumatism and neuralgia. It is a complex derivative of quinoline.
antiqueness: The quality of being antique; an appearance of ancient origin and workmanship. We may discover something venerable in the antiqueness of the work. Addison.
anthroposcopy: The art of discovering or judging of a man's character, passions. and inclinations from a study of his visible features.
antalkali: Anything that neutralizes, or that counteracts an alkaline tendency in the system. Hoopplw.
antipasch: The Sunday after Easter; Low Sunday.
androsphinx: A man sphinx; a sphinx having the head of a man and the body of a lion.
anthropopathic: Of or pertaining to anthropopathy. -- An`thro*po*path"ic*al*ly, adv. The daring anthropopathic imagery by which the prophets often represent God as chiding, upbraiding, threatening. H. Rogers.
antephialtic: Good against nightmare. -- n. A remedy nightmare. Dunglison.
antiquation: The act of making antiquated, or the state of being antiquated. Beaumont.
anamniotic: Without, or not developing, an amnion.
antihelix: The curved elevation of the cartilage of the ear, within or in front of the helix. See Ear.
anorthoscope: An optical toy for producing amusing figures or pictures by means of two revolving disks, on one of which distorted figures are painted.
antichristianity: Opposition or contrariety to the Christian religion.
anthropotomy: The anatomy or dissection of the human body; androtomy. Owen.
annodomini: In the year of the Christian era; as, a. d. 1887.
anticipative: Anticipating, or containing anticipation. "Anticipative of the feast to come." Cary. -- An*tic"i*pa*tive*ly, adv.
anabolic: Pertaining to anabolism; an anabolic changes, or processes, more or less constructive in their nature.
anticipatory: Forecasting; of the nature of anticipation. Owen. Here is an anticipatory glance of what was to be. J. C. Shairp.
animous: Full of spirit; hot; vehement; resolute. (old) Ash.
anilinism: A disease due to inhaling the poisonous fumes present in the manufacture of aniline.
antepredicament: A prerequisite to a clear understanding of the predicaments and categories, such as definitions of common terms. Chambers.
antiphysical: Contrary to nature; unnatural. | Relieving flatulence; carminative.
anisospore: A sexual spore in which the sexes differ in size; -- opposed to isospore.
anachronous: Containing an anachronism; anachronistic. -- An*ach"ro*nous*ly, adv.
antichrist: A denier or opponent of Christ. Specif.: A great antagonist, person or power, expected to precede Christ's second coming.
angelophany: The actual appearance of an angel to man.
antichthon: 1. A hypothetical earth counter to ours, or on the opposite side of the sun. Grote. 2. pl. Inhabitants of opposite hemispheres. Whewell.
anniversary: Returning with the year, at a stated time; annual; yearly; as, an anniversary feast. Anniversary day (R. C. Ch.). See Anniversary, n., 2. -- Anniversary week, that week in the year in which the… | 1. The annual return of the day on which any notable event took place, or is wont to be celebrated; as, the anniversary of the Declaration of Independence. 2. (R. C.
antepenult: The last syllable of a word except two, as -syl in monosyllable.
antithetical: Pertaining to antithesis, or opposition of words and sentiments; containing, or of the nature of, antithesis; contrasted.
anemone: 1. (Bot.) A genus of plants of the Ranunculus or Crowfoot family; windflower. Some of the species are cultivated in gardens. 2. (Zoöl.) The sea anemone. See Actinia, and Sea anemone. Note: This word is sometimes pronounced , especially by classical scholars.
anglify: To convert into English; to anglicize. Franklin. Darwin.
antimonious: Pertaining to, or derived from, antimony; -- said of those compounds of antimony in which this element has an equivalence next lower than the highest; as, antimonious acid.
antecedency: The state or condition of being antecedent; priority. Fothherby.
anchoretical: Pertaining to an anchoret or hermit; after the manner of an anchoret.
anatropal: Having the ovule inverted at an early period in its development, so that the chalaza is as the apparent apex; -- opposed to orthotropous. Gray.
antiputrescent: Counteracting, or preserving from, putrefaction; antiseptic.
anilic: Pertaining to, or obtained from, anil; indigotic; -- applied to an acid formed by the action of nitric acid on indigo.
anemograph: An instrument for measuring and recording the direction and force of the wind. Knight.
analyst: One who analyzes; formerly, one skilled in algebraical geometry; now commonly, one skilled in chemical analysis.
antihydropic: Good against dropsy. -- n. A remedy for dropsy.
antepone: To put before; to prefer. (old) Bailey.
anamnestic: Aiding the memory; as, anamnestic remedies.
antemeridian: Being before noon; in or pertaining to the forenoon. (Abbrev. a. m.)
anathematizer: One who pronounces an anathema. Hammond.
annulet: 1. A little ring. Tennyson. 2. (Arch.) A small, flat fillet, encircling a column, etc., used by itself, or with other moldings. It is used, several times repeated, under the Doric capital. 3. (Her.) A little circle borne as a charge. 4. (Zoöl.) A narrow circle of some distinct color on a surface or round an organ.
angelicalness: The quality of being angelic; excellence more than human.
antelucan: Held or being before light; -- a word applied to assemblies of Christians, in ancient times of persecution, held before light in the morning. "Antelucan worship." De Quincey.
anamese: Of or pertaining to Anam, to southeastern Asia. -- n. A native of Anam.
anglocatholic: Of or pertaining to a church modeled on the English Reformation; Anglican; -- sometimes restricted to the ritualistic or High Church section of the Church of England. | A member of the Church of England who contends for its catholic character; more specifically, a High Churchman.
analcime: A white or flesh-red mineral, of the zeolite, occurring in isometric crystals. By friction, it acquires a weak electricity; hence its name.
antimonsoon: The upper, contrary-moving current of the atmosphere over a monsoon.
antichristianism: Opposition or contrariety to the Christian religion.
ankle: The joint which connects the foot with the leg; the tarsus. Ankle bone, the bone of the ankle; the astragalus.
antiquated: Grown old. Hence: Bygone; obsolete; out of use; old-fashioned; as, an antiquated law. "Antiquated words." Dryden. Old Janet, for so he understood his antiquated attendant was denominated. Sir W. Scott. Syn. -- Ancient; old; antique; obsolete. See Ancient.
antifederalist: One of party opposed to a federative government; -- applied particularly to the party which opposed the adoption of the constitution of the United States. Pickering.
animistic: Of or pertaining to animism. Huxley. Tylor.
angiotomy: Dissection of the blood vessels and lymphatics of the body. Dunglison.
anabaptize: To rebaptize; to rechristen; also, to rename. Whitlock.
anchoret: One who renounces the world and secludes himself, usually for religious reasons; a hermit; a recluse. [Written by some authors anachoret.] Our Savior himself . . . did not choose an anchorite's or a monastic life, but a social and affable way of conversing with mortals. Boyle.
anecdotage: Anecdotes collectively; a collection of anecdotes. All history, therefore, being built partly, and some of it altogether, upon anecdotage, must be a tissue of lies. De Quincey.
analogical: 1. Founded on, or of the nature of, analogy; expressing or implying analogy. When a country which has sent out colonies is termed the mother country, the expression is analogical. J. S. Mill. 2. Having analogy; analogous. Sir M. Hale.
anchor: 1. anchoretism: The practice or mode of life of an anchoret.
anta: A species of pier produced by thickening a wall at its termination, treated architecturally as a pilaster, with capital and base. Note: Porches, when columns stand between two antæ, are called in Latin in antis.

animist: One who maintains the doctrine of animism.

anthracoid: Resembling anthrax in action; of the nature of anthrax; as, an anthracoid microbe.

anonymousness: The state or quality of being anonymous. Coleridge.

angelology: A discourse on angels, or a body of doctrines in regard to angels. The same mythology commanded the general consent; the same angelology, demonology. Milman.
angelet: A small gold coin formerly current in England; a half angel. Eng. Cyc.
anacamptically: By reflection; as, echoes are sound produced anacamptically. Hutton.
antichronism: Deviation from the true order of time; anachronism. Selden.
angleworm: A earthworm of the genus Lumbricus, frequently used by anglers for bait. See Earthworm.
antenumber: A number that precedes another. Bacon.
antidiphtheritic: Destructive to, or hindering the growth of, diphtheria bacilli. -- n. An antidiphtheritic agent.
antalgic: Alleviating pain. -- n. A medicine to alleviate pain; an anodyne.

andesine: A kind of triclinic feldspar found in the Andes.
anthesis: The period or state of full expansion in a flower. Gray.

antiscriptural: Opposed to, or not in accordance with, the Holy Scriptures.
anil: A West Indian plant (Indigofera anil), one of the original sources of indigo; also, the indigo dye.
anapophysis: An accessory process in many lumbar vertebræ.

anopla: One of the two orders of Nemerteans. See Nemertina.
anaglyptic: Relating to the art of carving, enchasing, or embossing in low relief.
anew: Over again; another time; in a new form; afresh; as, to arm anew; to create anew. Dryden.

annueler: A priest employed in saying annuals, or anniversary Masses. (old) Chaucer.

animalism: The state, activity, or enjoyment of animals; mere animal life without intellectual or moral qualities; sensuality.

antipetalous: Standing before a petal, as a stamen.
anelectrode: The positive pole of a voltaic battery.
antisolar: Opposite to the sun; -- said of the point in the heavens 180º distant from the sun.
anan: An expression equivalent to What did you say Sir Eh (old) Shak.

annumeration: Addition to a former number. (old) Sir T. Browne.

antaean: Pertaining to Antæus, a giant athlete slain by Hercules.
antiparallels: Straight lines or planes which make angles in some respect opposite in character to those made by parallel lines or planes.
antitropal: At the extremity most remote from the hilum, as the embryo, or inverted with respect to the seed, as the radicle. Lindley.
antenicene: Of or in the Christian church or era, anterior to the first council of Nice, held a. d. 325; as, antenicene faith.
anticausotic: Good against an inflammatory fever. -- n. A remedy for such a fever.
antiparalytic: Good against paralysis. -- n. A medicine for paralysis.
anthelmintic: Good against intestinal worms. -- An anthelmintic remedy. [Written also anthelminthic.]
angelica: 1. antipyic: Checking or preventing suppuration. -- n. An antipyic medicine.
anointment: The act of anointing, or state of being anointed; also, an ointment. Milton.
antic: 1. Old; antique. (Zoöl.) "Lords of antic fame." Phaer. 2. Odd; fantastic; fanciful; grotesque; ludicrous. The antic postures of a merry-andrew. Addison. The Saxons . . . | 1. antepenultimate: Of or pertaining to the last syllable but two. -- n. The antepenult.

animalculum: An animalcule. Note: Animalculæ, as if from a Latin singular animalcula, is a barbarism.
ancientness: The quality of being ancient; antiquity; existence from old times.
anthropologist: One who is versed in anthropology.
antagony: Contest; opposition; antagonism. (old) Antagony that is between Christ and Belial. Milton.
antipathetic: Having a natural contrariety, or constitutional aversion, to a thing; characterized by antipathy; -- often followed by to. Fuller.

annunciative: Pertaining to annunciation; announcing. Dr. H. More.
anchorless: Without an anchor or stay. Hence: Drifting; unsettled.
anthem: 1. Formerly, a hymn sung in alternate parts, in present usage, a selection from the Psalms, or other parts of the Scriptures or the liturgy, set to sacred music. 2. A song or hymn of praise. Milton. | To celebrate with anthems. [Poet.] Sweet birds antheming the morn. Keats.
anna: An East Indian money of account, the sixteenth of a rupee, or about 2
animalculist: 1. One versed in the knowledge of animalcules. Keith. 2. A believer in the theory of animalculism.
anisotropic: Not isotropic; having different properties in different directions; thus, crystals of the isometric system are optically isotropic, but all other crystals are anisotropic.
anabas: A genus of fishes, remarkable for their power of living long out of water, and of making their way on land for considerable distances, and for climbing trees; the climbing fishes.
anthropoidea: The suborder of primates which includes the monkeys, apes, and man.
anadrom: A fish that leaves the sea and ascends rivers.
angienchyma: Vascular tissue of plants, consisting of spiral vessels, dotted, barred, and pitted ducts, and laticiferous vessels.
antiamerican: Opposed to the Americans, their aims, or interests, or to the genius of American institutions. Marshall.
anchorite: One who renounces the world and secludes himself, usually for religious reasons; a hermit; a recluse. [Written by some authors anachoret.] Our Savior himself . . . did not choose an anchorite's or a monastic life, but a social and affable way of conversing with mortals. Boyle.
antirenter: One opposed to the payment of rent; esp. one of those who in 1840-47 resisted the collection of rents claimed by the patroons from the settlers on certain manorial lands in the State of New York. -- An`ti*rent"ism, n.
angry: 1. Troublesome; vexatious; rigorous. (old) God had provided a severe and angry education to chastise the forwardness of a young spirit. Jer. Taylor. 2. Inflamed and painful, as a sore. 3. annihilationist: One who believes that eternal punishment consists in annihilation or extinction of being; a destructionist.
anaesthesia: Entire or partial loss or absence of feeling or sensation; a state of general or local insensibility produced by disease or by the inhalation or application of an anæsthetic.

antiquarianism: Character of an antiquary; study or love of antiquities. Warburton.

annuent: Nodding; as, annuent muscles (used in nodding).
anthropomorphosis: Transformation into the form of a human being.

annotative: Characterized by annotations; of the nature of annotation.
analgesia: Absence of sensibility to pain. Quain.
antiperiodic: A remedy possessing the property of preventing the return of periodic paroxysms, or exacerbations, of disease, as in intermittent fevers.
anciently: 1. In ancient times. 2. In an ancient manner.
aniseed: The seed of the anise; also, a cordial prepared from it. "Oil of aniseed." Brande & C.
anaesthetization: The process of anæsthetizing; also, the condition of the nervous system induced by anæsthetics.
anaclastic: 1. (Opt.) Produced by the refraction of light, as seen through water; as, anaclastic curves. 2. Springing back, as the bottom of an anaclastic glass. ancipitous: Two-edged instead of round; -- said of certain flattened stems, as those of blue grass, and rarely also of leaves.
anthodium: The inflorescence of a compound flower in which many florets are gathered into a involucrate head.
anathematize: To pronounce an anathema against; to curse. Hence: To condemn publicly as something accursed. Milton.
annelida: A division of the Articulata, having the body formed of numerous rings or annular segments, and without jointed legs. The principal subdivisions are the Chætopoda, including the Oligochæta or earthworms and Polychæta or marine worms; and the Hirudinea or leeches. See Chætopoda.
anticlastic: Having to opposite curvatures, that is, curved longitudinally in one direction and transversely in the opposite direction, as the surface of a saddle.
antevert: 1. To prevent. (old) Bp. Hall. 2. (Med.) To displace by anteversion.

anothergaines: Of another kind. (old) Sir P. Sidney.
anaemia: A morbid condition in which the blood is deficient in quality or in quantity.
anachronize: To refer to, or put into, a wrong time. Lowell.
annotation: A note, added by way of comment, or explanation; -- usually in the plural; as, annotations on ancient authors, or on a word or a passage.

anisodactyls: (a) A group of herbivorous mammals characterized by having the hoofs in a single series around the foot, as the elephant, rhinoceros, etc. (b) A group of perching birds which are anisodactylous.

anas: A genus of water fowls, of the order Anseres, including certain species of fresh-water ducks.
ancestral: Of, pertaining to, derived from, or possessed by, an ancestor or ancestors; as, an ancestral estate. "Ancestral trees." Hemans.
anaptotic: Having lost, or tending to lose, inflections by phonetic decay; as, anaptotic languages.
anisotrope: Not isotropic; having different properties in different directions; thus, crystals of the isometric system are optically isotropic, but all other crystals are anisotropic.
anacamptics: 1. The science of reflected light, now called catoptrics. 2. The science of reflected sounds.
anthropomorphous: Having the figure of, or resemblance to, a man; as, an anthromorphous plant. "Anthromorphous apes." Darwin.
animalization: 1. The act of animalizing; the giving of animal life, or endowing with animal properties. 2. Conversion into animal matter by the process of assimilation. Owen.
antistrophic: Of or pertaining to an antistrophe.
anisopleura: A primary division of gastropods, including those having spiral shells. The two sides of the body are unequally developed.
annelidous: Of the nature of an annelid.
annealing: 1. The process used to render glass, iron, etc., less brittle, performed by allowing them to cool very gradually from a high heat. 2. The burning of metallic colors into glass, earthenware, etc.
anenst: 1. Over against; as, he lives anent the church. 2. About; concerning; in respect; as, he said nothing anent this particular.
antrum: A cavern or cavity, esp. an anatomical cavity or sinus. Huxley.
antorbital: Pertaining to, or situated in, the region of the front of the orbit. -- n. The antorbital bone.
antipathic: Belonging to antipathy; opposite; contrary; allopathic.

antozone: A compound formerly supposed to be modification of oxygen, but now known to be hydrogen dioxide; -- so called because apparently antagonistic to ozone, converting it into ordinary oxygen.
anadem: A garland or fillet; a chaplet or wreath. Drayton. Tennyson.

antiquity: 1. The quality of being ancient; ancientness; great age; as, a statue of remarkable antiquity; a family of great antiquity. 2. Old age. (old) It not your voice broken . . . and every part about you blasted with antiquity Shak. 3. Ancient times; former ages; times long since past; as, Cicero was an eloquent orator of antiquity. 4. The ancients; the people of ancient times.
anseriformes: A division of birds including the geese, ducks, and closely allied forms.
antithet: An antithetic or contrasted statement. Bacon.
anisomeric: Not isomeric; not made of the same components in the same proportions.
anonym: 1. One who is anonymous; also sometimes used for "pseudonym." 2. A notion which has no name, or which can not be expressed by a single English word. J. R. Seeley.
answerably: In an answerable manner; in due proportion or correspondence; suitably.
anglian: Of or pertaining to the Angles. -- n. One of the Angles.
antilithic: Tending to prevent the formation of urinary calculi, or to destroy them when formed. -- n. An antilithic medicine.
animal: 1. An organized living being endowed with sensation and the power of voluntary motion, and also characterized by taking its food into an internal cavity or stomach for digestion; | 1. Of or relating to animals; as, animal functions. 2. Pertaining to the merely sentient part of a creature, as distinguished from the intellectual, rational, or spiritual part;
anorexia: Want of appetite, without a loathing of food. Coxe.
annoyer: One who, or that which, annoys.
anophyte: A moss or mosslike plant which cellular stems, having usually an upward growth and distinct leaves.
antipsoric: Of use in curing the itch. -- n. An antipsoric remedy.
annulary: Having the form of a ring; annular. Ray.
analytical: Of or pertaining to analysis; resolving into elements or constituent parts; as, an analytical experiment; analytic reasoning; -- opposed to synthetic. Analytical or coördinate geometry. See under Geometry. -- Analytic language, a noninflectional language or one not characterized by grammatical endings. -- Analytical table (Nat.
anthraquinone: A hydrocarbon, C6H4.C2O2.C6H4, subliming in shining yellow needles. It is obtained by oxidation of anthracene.
anaerobies: Microörganisms which do not require oxygen, but are killed by it. Sternberg.
anthropometry: Measurement of the height and other dimensions of human beings, especially at different ages, or in different races, occupations, etc. Dunglison.
antiphonal: Of or pertaining to antiphony, or alternate singing; sung alternately by a divided choir or opposite choirs. Wheatly. -- An*tiph"o*nal*ly, adv. | A book of antiphons or anthems.
antonym: A word of opposite meaning; a counterterm; -- used as a correlative of synonym. C. J. Smith.
androgynal: 1. Uniting both sexes in one, or having the characteristics of both; being in nature both male and female; hermaphroditic. Owen. The truth is, a great mind must be androgynous. Coleridge. 2. (Bot.) Bearing both staminiferous and pistilliferous flowers in the same cluster.
animosity: 1. Mere spiritedness or courage. (old) Skelton. Such as give some proof of animosity, audacity, and execution, those she [the crocodile] loveth. Holland. 2. Violent hatred leading to active opposition; active enmity; energetic dislike. Macaulay. Syn. -- Enmity; hatred; opposition. -- Animosity, Enmity. Enmity be dormant or concealed;
aneurism: A soft, pulsating, hollow tumor, containing blood, arising from the preternatural dilation or rupture of the coats of an artery. [Written also aneurysm.]
anthropomorphize: To attribute a human form or personality to. You may see imaginative children every day anthropomorphizing. Lowell.
anything: 1. Any object, act, state, event, or fact whatever; thing of any kind; something or other; aught; as, I would not do it for anything. Did you ever know of anything so unlucky A. Trollope. | In any measure; anywise; at all. Mine old good will and hearty affection towards you is not . . . anything at all quailed. Robynson (More's Utopia).
anterior: 1. Before in time; antecedent. Antigonus, who was anterior to Polybius. Sir G. C. Lewis. 2. Before, or toward the front, in place; as, the anterior part of the mouth; -- opposed to posterior. Note: In comparative anatomy, anterior often signifies at or toward the head, cephalic; and in human anatomy it is often used for ventral. Syn. -- Antecedent; previous; precedent;
analogism: 1. Logic an argument from the cause to the effect; an a priori argument. Johnson. 2. Investigation of things by the analogy they bear to each other. Crabb.
anastigmatic: Not astigmatic; --said esp. of a lens system which consists of a converging lens and a diverging lens of equal and opposite astigmatism but different focal lengths, and sensibly free from astigmatism.
androtomy: Dissection of the human body, as distinguished from zoötomy; anthropotomy.
antetemple: The portico, or narthex in an ancient temple or church.
angleofincidence: The angle between the chord of an aërocurve and the relative direction of the undisturbed air current.
anthocarpous: Having some portion of the floral envelopes attached to the pericarp to form the fruit, as in the checkerberry, the mulberry, and the pineapple.
anguilliform: Eel-shaped. Note: The "Anguillæformes" of Cuvier are fishes related to thee eel.
anthozoic: Of or pertaining to the Anthozoa.
antitypical: Of or pertaining to an antitype; explaining the type. -- An`ti*typ"ic*al*ly, adv.
anywise: In any wise or way; at all. "Anywise essential." Burke.
antares: The principal star in Scorpio: -- called also the Scorpion's Heart.
animadversion: 1. The act or power of perceiving or taking notice; direct or simple perception. (old) The soul is the sole percipient which hath animadversion and sense, properly so called. Glanvill. 2. Monition; warning. (old) Clarendon. 3. Remarks by way of criticism and usually of censure; adverse criticism; reproof; blame.
antimephitic: Good against mephitic or deletplwious gases. -- n. A remedy against mephitic gases. Dunglison.
antependium: The hangings or screen in front of the altar; an altar cloth; the frontal. Smollett.
anhydrous: Destitute of water; as, anhydrous salts or acids.
ancony: A piece of malleable iron, wrought into the shape of a bar in the middle, but unwrought at the ends.
anginose: Pertaining to angina or angina pectoris.
anicut: A dam or mole made in the course of a stream for the purpose of regulating the flow of a system of irrigation. [India] Brande & C.
anemometer: An instrument for measuring the force or velocity of the wind; a wind gauge.
antibacchius: A foot of three syllables, the first two long, and the last short.
andropetalous: Produced by the conversion of the stamens into petals, as double flowers, like the garden ranunculus. Brande.
antecedent: 1. Going before in time; prior; anterior; preceding; as, an event antecedent to the Deluge; an antecedent cause. 2. Presumptive; as, an antecedent improbability. Syn. -- Prior; previous; foregoing. | 1. That which goes before in time; that which precedes. South. The Homeric mythology, as well as the Homeric language, has surely its antecedents. Max Miller. 2. One who precedes or goes in front.
anteflexion: A displacement forward of an organ, esp. the uterus, in such manner that its axis is bent upon itself. T. G. Thomas.
antimask: A secondary mask, or grotesque interlude, between the parts of a serious mask. [Written also anue.] Bacon.
anastate: One of a series of substances formed, in secreting cells, by constructive or anabolic processes, in the production of protoplasm; -- opposed to katastate. Foster.
anacanthini: A group of teleostean fishes destitute of spiny fin-rays, as the cod.
anomalous: Deviating from a general rule, method, or analogy; abnormal; irregular; as, an anomalous proceeding.
antisemitism: Opposition to, or hatred of, Semites, esp. Jews. -- An`ti- Sem"ite (#), n. -- An`ti-Sem*it"ic (#), a.
antagonize: To contend with; to oppose actively; to counteract.
anaplerotic: Filling up; promoting granulation of wounds or ulcers. -- n. A remedy which promotes such granulation.
anchorwatch: A detail of one or more men who keep watch on deck at night when a vessel is at anchor.
antibrachium: That part of the fore limb between the brachium and the carpus; the forearm.
anserous: Resembling a goose; silly; simple. Sydney Smith.
ancipital: Two-edged instead of round; -- said of certain flattened stems, as those of blue grass, and rarely also of leaves.
anabolism: The constructive metabolism of the body, as distinguished from katabolism.
antecedaneous: Antecedent; preceding in time. "Capable of antecedaneous proof." Barrow.
antoeci: Those who live under the same meridian, but on opposite parallels of latitude, north and south of the equator.
anomuran: Irregular in the character of the tail or abdomen; as, the anomural crustaceans. [Written also anomoural, anomouran.]
anglicanism: 1. Strong partiality to the principles and rites of the Church of England. 2. The principles of the established church of England; also, in a restricted sense, the doctrines held by the high-church party. 3. Attachment to England or English institutions.
anthroponomics: The science of the laws of the development of the human organism in relation to other organisms and to environment. -- An`thro*po*nom"ic*al (#), a.
anthorism: A description or definition contrary to that which is given by the adverse party.
angosturabark: An aromatic bark used as a tonic, obtained from a South American of the rue family (Galipea cusparia, or officinalis). U. S. Disp.
antecedently: Previously; before in time; at a time preceding; as, antecedently to conversion. Barrow.
annulment: The act of annulling; abolition; invalidation.
angwantibo: A small lemuroid mammal (Arctocebus Calabarensis) of Africa. It has only a rudimentary tail.
antonomastic: Pertaining to, or characterized by, antonomasia. -- An`to*no*mas"tic*al*ly, adv.
anchusin: A resinoid coloring matter obtained from alkanet root.
anconal: Of or pertaining to the ancon or elbow. "The olecranon on anconeal process." Flower.
animated: Endowed with life; full of life or spirit; indicating animation; lively; vigorous. "Animated sounds." Pope. "Animated bust." Gray. "Animated descriptions." Lewis.
anonymity: The quality or state of being anonymous; anonymousness; also, that which anonymous. He rigorously insisted upon the rights of anonymity. Carlyle.
angiopathy: Disease of the vessels, esp. the blood vessels.
anticivism: Opposition to the body politic of citizens. (old) Carlyle.
anal: Pertaining to, or situated near, the anus; as, the anal fin or glands.
antitropous: At the extremity most remote from the hilum, as the embryo, or inverted with respect to the seed, as the radicle. Lindley.
anchylosis: 1. (Med.) Stiffness or fixation of a joint; formation of a stiff joint. Dunglison. 2. (Anat.) The union of two or more separate bones to from a single bone; the close union of bones or other structures in various animals.
anonaceous: Pertaining to the order of plants including the soursop, custard apple, etc.
anthropomorphism: 1. The representation of the Deity, or of a polytheistic deity, under a human form, or with human attributes and affections. 2. The ascription of human characteristics to things not human.
anhydride: An oxide of a nonmetallic body or an organic radical, capable of forming an acid by uniting with the elements of water; -- so called because it may be formed from an acid by the abstraction of water.
anisodactylous: Characterized by unequal toes, three turned forward and one backward, as in most passerine birds.
antiperistaltic: Opposed to, or checking motion; acting upward; -- applied to an inverted action of the intestinal tube.
anecdotal: Pertaining to, or abounding with, anecdotes; as, anecdotal conversation.
anywhither: To or towards any place. (old) De Foe.
anticathode: The part of a vacuum tube opposite the cathode. Upon it the cathode rays impinge.
anchorhold: 1. The hold or grip of an anchor, or that to which it holds. 2. Hence: Firm hold: security.
antitragus: A prominence on the lower posterior portion of the concha of the external ear, opposite the tragus. See Ear.
anguine: Of, pertaining to, or resembling, a snake or serpent. "The anguine or snakelike reptiles." Owen.
angulometer: An instrument for measuring external angles.
animastic: Pertaining to mind or spirit; spiritual.
anabaptistry: The doctrine, system, or practice, of Anabaptists. Thus died this imaginary king; and Anabaptistry was suppressed in Munster. Pagitt.
anisopoda: A division of Crustacea, which, in some its characteristics, is intermediate between Amphipoda and Isopoda.
anglicization: The act of anglicizing, or making English in character.
anthropogeography: The science of the human species as to geographical distribution and environment. Broadly, it includes industrial, commercial, and political geography, and that part of ethnology which deals with distribution and physical environment. -- An`thro*po*ge*og"ra*pher (#), n. -- An`thro*po*ge`o*graph"ic*al (#), a.
antherogenous: Transformed from anthers, as the petals of a double flower.
antheridium: The male reproductive apparatus in the lower, consisting of a cell or other cavity in which spermatozoids are produced; -- called also spermary. -- An`ther*id"i*al, a.
angled: Having an angle or angles; -- used in compounds; as, right- angled, many-angled, etc. The thrice three-angled beechnut shell. Bp. Hall.
anthozoa: The class of the Coelenterata which includes the corals and sea anemones. The three principal groups or orders are Acyonaria, Actinaria, and Madreporaria.
angel: 1. A messenger. The dear good angel of the Spring, The nightingale. B. Jonson. 2. A spiritual, celestial being, superior to man in power and intelligence. In the Scriptures the angels appear as God's messengers. O, welcome, pure-eyed Faith, white-handed Hope, Thou hovering angel, girt with golden wings. Milton. 3. One of a class of "fallen angels;" an evil spirit;
animadversive: Having the power of perceiving; percipient. (old) Glanvill. I do not mean there is a certain number of ideas glaring and shining to the animadversive faculty. Coleridge.
anachronic: Characterized by, or involving, anachronism; anachronistic.
anthracometric: Of or pertaining to an anthracometer.
antiicteric: Good against jaundice. -- n. A remedy for jaundice.
antipyrotic: Good against burns or pyrosis. -- n. Anything of use in preventing or healing burns or pyrosis.
antimagistrical: Opposed to the office or authority of magistrates. (old) South.
another: 1. One more, in addition to a former number; a second or additional one, similar in likeness or in effect. Another yet! -- a seventh! I 'll see no more. Shak. Would serve to scale another Hero's tower. Shak. 2. Not the same; different. He winks, and turns his lips another way. Shak. 3. Any or some; any different person, indefinitely; any one else; some one else.
anarchical: Pertaining to anarchy; without rule or government; in political confusion; tending to produce anarchy; as, anarchic despotism; anarchical opinions.
annihilation: 1. The act of reducing to nothing, or nonexistence; or the act of destroying the form or combination of parts under which a thing exists, so that the name can no longer be applied to it; as, the annihilation of a corporation. 2. The state of being annihilated. Hooker.
antbird: See Ant bird, under Ant, n.
anglo: A combining form meaning the same as English; or English and, or English conjoined with; as, Anglo-Turkish treaty, Anglo-German, Anglo-Irish. Anglo-American, . Of or pertaining to the English and Americans, or to the descendants of Englishmen in America. -- n. A descendant from English ancestors born in America, or the United States. Anglo-Danish, a.
androgyny: Union of both sexes in one individual; hermaphroditism.
antanaclasis: (a) A figure which consists in repeating the same word in a different sense; as, Learn some craft when young, that when old you may live without craft. (b) A repetition of words beginning a sentence, after a long parenthesis; as, Shall that heart (which not only feels them, but which has all motions of life placed in them), shall that heart, etc.
anallagmatic: Not changed in form by inversion. Anallagmatic curves, a class of curves of the fourth degree which have certain peculiar relations to circles; -- sometimes called bicircular quartics. -- Anallagmatic surfaces, a certain class of surfaces of the fourth degree.
annulus: 1. A ring; a ringlike part or space. 2. (Geom.) (a) A space contained between the circumferences of two circles, one within the other. (b) The solid formed by a circle revolving around a line which is the plane of the circle but does not cut it. 3. (Zoöl.) Ring-shaped structures or markings, found in, or upon, various animals.
angulate: Having angles or corners; angled; as, angulate leaves.
anthophyllite: A mineral of the hornblende group, of a yellowish gray or clove brown color. -- An`tho*phyl*lit"ic, a.
antestomach: A cavity which leads into the stomach, as in birds. Ray.
antisabbatarian: One of a sect which opposes the observance of the Christian Sabbath.
anoint: 1. To smear or rub over with oil or an unctuous substance; also, to spread over, as oil. And fragrant oils the stiffened limbs anoint. Dryden. He anointed the eyes of the blind man with the clay. John ix. 6. 2. To apply oil to or to pour oil upon, etc., as a sacred rite, especially for consecration.
animalize: 1. To endow with the properties of an animal; to represent in animal form. Warburton. 2. To convert into animal matter by the processes of assimilation. 3. To render animal or sentient; to reduce to the state of a lower animal; to sensualize. The unconscious irony of the Epicurean poet on the animalizing tendency of his own philosophy. Coleridge.
anatomically: In an anatomical manner; by means of dissection.
anthracomancy: Divination by inspecting a burning coal.
anagrammatical: Pertaining to, containing, or making, anagram. -- An`a*gram*mat"ic*al*ly, adv.
anientise: To frustrate; to bring to naught; to annihilate. (old) Chaucer.
ankylostomiasis: A disease due to the presence of the parasites Agchylostoma duodenale, Uncinaria (subgenus Necator) americana, or allied nematodes, in the small intestine. When present in large numbers they produce a severe anæmia by sucking the blood from the intestinal walls. Called also miner's anæmia, tunnel disease, brickmaker's anæmia, Egyptian chlorosis.
anemography: 1. A description of the winds. 2. The art of recording the direction and force of the wind, as by means of an anemograph.
annelid: Of or pertaining to the Annelida. -- n. One of the Annelida.
annuloid: Of or pertaining to the Annuloida.
ankerite: A mineral closely related to dolomite, but containing iron.
anthemis: Chamomile; a genus of composite, herbaceous plants.
anthraceneoil: A heavy green oil (partially solidifying on cooling), which distills over from coal tar at a temperature above 270º. It is the principal source of anthracene.
anergia: Lack of energy; inactivity. -- An*er"gic (#), a.
annotinous: A year old; in Yearly growths.
antimonial: Of or pertaining to antimony. -- n. (Med.) A preparation or medicine containing antimony. Antimonial powder, a consisting of one part oxide of antimony and two parts phosphate of calcium; -- also called James's powder.
anomalistical: 1. Irregular; departing from common or established rules. 2. (Astron.) Pertaining to the anomaly, or angular distance of a planet from its perihelion. Anomalistic month. See under Month. -- Anomalistic revolution, the period in which a planet or satellite goes through the complete cycles of its changes of anomaly, or from any point in its elliptic orbit to the same again.
antibillous: Counteractive of bilious complaints; tending to relieve biliousness.
anaglyptography: The art of copying works in relief, or of engraving as to give the subject an embossed or raised appearance; -- used in representing coins, bas-reliefs, etc.
anisic: Of or derived from anise; as, anisic acid; anisic alcohol.
anathematization: The act of anathematizing, or denouncing as accursed; imprecation. Barrow.
anencephalic: Without a brain; brainless. Todd & B.
anomura: A group of decapod Crustacea, of which the hermit crab in an example.
antimonite: 1. (Chem.) A compound of antimonious acid and a base or basic radical. 2. (Min.) Stibnite.
